The Trump administration intends to deploy drones to South America ahead of planned operations on the continent targeting drug trafficking and terrorism, according to a new report.

MQ-9 Reaper drones based out of Africa are expected to be transferred to U.S. Southern Command, which oversees operations in Latin America, half a dozen sources with knowledge of the matter told CNN.

The remotely piloted aircraft — which cost $56 million apiece — are primarily used for intelligence gathering, though they can also be used to carry out precision strikes, according to the Air Force.

While the number of drones slated for relocation from Africa remains unknown, one source told CNN that “most” would be reassigned to South America, where the Trump administration has sought to exert extraordinary influence.

The move highlights the tradeoffs confronting a military stretched across multiple regions. In Africa, concerns about terrorism — including from ISIS — remain present. In the Middle East, questions have been raised about the supply of MQ-9 Reaper drones after at least 45 aircraft, or about 25 percent of the fleet, were reportedly lost in the Iran war.

open image in gallery The US military may soon deploy MQ-9 Reaper drones to South America ahead of planned counterterrorism and counternarcotics operations, according to a new report ( U.S. Air Force via Getty Images )

The Independent has contacted the Pentagon for comment.

Since returning to office, Trump has pursued an aggressive policy to establish U.S. dominance in the Western Hemisphere — an approach that has been dubbed the “Donroe Doctrine.”

For instance, last September, his administration began striking alleged drug boats near the continent, which have resulted in the deaths of at least 230 people. In January, U.S. special forces captured then-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife during an operation in Caracas.

Trump’s supporters have hailed the moves as a forceful assertion of U.S. interests, while critics have condemned them as brazenly unlawful.

CNN also previously reported that the Justice Department had drafted a legal opinion last year that permits the U.S. military to carry out lethal action against alleged drug traffickers and cartels, citing an imminent threat to Americans.

open image in gallery During an August visit to Panama, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth thanked Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Colombia and Jamaica for partnering with the US in military operations targeting ‘narco-terrorists’ in those nations ( AFP via Getty Images )

More recently, U.S. officials have sought to expand their operations by forging security partnerships with governments across Latin America.

During an August visit to Panama, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth thanked Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Colombia and Jamaica for partnering with the U.S. in military operations targeting “narco-terrorists” in those nations.

Some operations have already taken place.

In March, the Pentagon announced that the U.S. had “executed targeted action” against “narco-terrorism networks” in Ecuador in partnership with the country’s government. “We are bombing Narco Terrorists on land as well,” Hegseth boasted at the time.

A subsequent investigation by The New York Times indicates that the bombed‑out site had no connection to drug trafficking and appears to have been a small dairy and cattle farm.

In recent weeks, the U.S. has also reached agreements with Colombia and Panama to send drones to both countries, including for drug-trafficking surveillance.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Friday cast Canada as moving quickly beyond its historical reliance on the United States after a whirlwind week in which he embraced the prospect of becoming the European Union’s first associate member.

Carney, who returned from Europe on Thursday night, said Canada and Europe had “launched a process for a new alliance.” He also called the latest U.S. tariffs a “miscalculation” and repeated that suspending trade talks with Washington last month was the right decision.

“Amidst this global rupture, we must move forward,” Carney said.

He spoke Friday to Liberal lawmakers gathered in Ottawa ahead of a new session of Parliament, his first public remarks since returning Thursday evening from Strasbourg.

A day after telling the European Parliament that Canada and Europe needed greater resilience so no country could control their markets, impair their sovereignty or dictate their choices, Carney pointed Friday to Canada’s fiscal position as another source of strength.

Carney, a former head of the central banks of both Canada and England, also appeared to contrast Canada with the United States as U.S. government borrowing costs remain significantly higher than Canada’s.

“We’re now seeing financial markets starting to change the pricing ... to separate the strong from the weak,” Carney said. “We are the strong. We are Canada strong.”

The remarks capped a seven-day stretch in which he hosted Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, convened major global investors in Toronto, met new U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Liverpool and addressed the European Parliament.

In Strasbourg, Carney embraced a shift toward Europe, calling for a far deeper alliance spanning energy, critical minerals, defense, artificial intelligence, research and other strategic sectors where he says Canada can no longer afford to depend on a single country.

The next major step is an Oct. 29-30 Canada-EU summit in Montreal.

President Donald Trump has imposed tariffs on Canadian goods, repeatedly talked about making Canada the 51st state and threatened additional economic measures. Trade negotiations collapsed last month and remain suspended.

Carney also touted a business tax break announced at this week’s Canada Investment Summit that is expected to cut the effective tax rate on new investment to 6.4%, less than half the U.S. rate.

“We didn’t need a big beautiful bill. We needed a targeted initiative,” Carney said, drawing laughter with an apparent jab at Trump’s signature tax-and-spending law.

Carney also appeared to mimic Trump while boasting that a major clean-energy project would produce the equivalent of “18 Hoover Dams,” repeating the phrase as he twice used the president’s familiar accordionlike hand gesture.

The government announced nearly half a trillion dollars in investment commitments around the summit.

“In the last seven days, we have stood shoulder to shoulder with an ally, we’ve catalyzed record investment into our country, we’ve deepened our ties with Europe,” Carney said.

“It’s a lot, but that was the warm-up.”

News.title: Cops race to find stolen $50K bronze Jesus statue before it’s lost forever
News.content:

Police in Southern California are searching for two men who severed and stole a $50,000 bronze Jesus statue from a church campus, leaving only the feet behind on its stone base.

Concerns are growing that the thieves may attempt to melt down the religious artwork to sell the raw metal.

Surveillance video captured two suspects wearing dark clothing arriving at Christ Our Savior Catholic Church in Santa Ana at roughly 2 a.m. on August 30. The men brought a bag onto the property, extracted an electric cutting tool and sliced through the sculpture at its ankles, according to the Santa Ana Police Department.

“One of the suspects retrieves a cutting tool from the bag, and both suspects begin to cut the Jesus statue from its feet, dragging it through the property,” a Santa Ana police spokesperson told local outlet KTLA.

After freeing the sculpture — which depicted Jesus with his hands clasped in prayer near John the Baptist — the suspects hauled it across the church grounds toward nearby Segerstrom High School. Authorities believe a getaway vehicle was waiting near the school, where the men loaded the piece inside and fled.

Authorities in Santa Ana, California, are searching for two men who cut down a $50,000 bronze Jesus statue from a Catholic church campus, leaving only its feet attached to the stone base ( Santa Ana Police Department )

Images published by the Santa Ana Police Department show the remnants of the display: two hollow bronze, barefoot feet still attached to the rock. The department noted that the property had been targeted in past incidents.

Images published by the Santa Ana Police Department show the remnants of the display: two hollow bronze, barefoot feet still attached to the rock. The August theft follows a prior incident on April 22, when suspects damaged wooden fence panels to break onto the church grounds and cut portions of the same bronze statue, causing thousands of dollars in property damage, as reported by News Santa Ana.

“Unfortunately, this church was targeted once again, but this time, two suspects successfully stole a $50,000 bronze statue of Jesus,” the department wrote in a Facebook post.

Police released surveillance footage in hopes that the public could help identify the suspects. Though one suspect kept his face covered, another was filmed wearing a distinct T-shirt that investigators hope someone will recognize.

Anyone with information is urged to contact Detective R. Wilson at 714-245-8551 or RashadWilson@santa-ana.org.

It’s game on for GameStop, once again.

Some shuttered locations are reopening with the first confirmed store at 4756 Ridge Road in Brooklyn, Ohio, a company spokesperson told The Independent Friday.

“As for the rest, stay tuned,” the spokesperson added.

The confirmation comes after GameStop, which became a symbol of the 2021 meme-stock craze, announced last week that some stores would begin reopening September 11.

The retailer has not released a complete list or number of locations set to return. As of January 27, 2026, there were 2,086 GameStop stores in the U.S., according to data company ScrapeHero.

open image in gallery A GameStop in Brooklyn, Ohio, was the first shuttered location to reopen September 11 as part of a surprise nationwide rollout ( GameStop )

The store reopenings come about nine months after GameStop announced plans to close locations across several states as part of its efforts to cut costs and adjust to changing shopping habits.

While GameStop did not release a complete list of stores slated for closure in January, local media reports and customer notices indicated that locations in Ohio, Illinois, New York, Kansas, Kentucky, Connecticut and Minnesota were among those that had either closed or were preparing to shut down.

The closures followed GameStop’s downsizing efforts, which resulted in 590 U.S. stores closing during the company’s 2025 fiscal year, which ended January 31, 2026, according to Fast Company. GameStop said the closures were part of a “store portfolio optimization review.”

In a December SEC filing, GameStop also said it planned to close a “significant number” of additional stores during the fiscal year.

The reopenings come as GameStop’s top executives invest in the company and the retailer continues shifting its business toward collectibles. CEO Ryan Cohen bought 1 million shares of GameStop stock September 10, paying an average of about $20.38 per share, Fox Business reports.

The purchase was worth about $20.4 million, according to federal filings cited by the outlet. GameStop board member Alain Attal also bought 5,000 shares that day, worth about $100,000.

open image in gallery GameStop has not released a full list of shuttered stores set to reopen or said where the next revived locations will be ( Getty )

Meanwhile, collectibles are becoming a bigger part of GameStop’s business. Trading cards and other collectibles made up 45.1 percent of the company’s sales in its most recent quarter, up from about 29 percent in fiscal 2025, per Fox Business. Collectibles sales were also 57 percent higher than they were during the same quarter a year earlier.

GameStop’s stock has remained volatile since its explosive rise in 2021 and has never returned to the highs reached during the meme-stock frenzy. Over the past year, the company’s shares have fallen about 36 percent, according to Fast Company.

GameStop became one of the biggest names of the 2021 meme-stock boom after everyday investors, many of them organizing on Reddit’s r/WallStreetBets, helped push its stock from less than $20 to more than $480 at its peak.

The dramatic rise was fueled in part by a short squeeze, which put pressure on hedge funds that had bet the stock would fall. Elon Musk also helped draw attention to GameStop with a tweet about the company. The sudden surge led to trading halts, major losses for some investors and scrutiny of how the stock market operates.

The frenzy eventually prompted congressional hearings and renewed debate over market rules and the role of retail investors.

News.title: GPs summoned in Frankfurt as third malaria death reported
News.content:
While malaria is treatable if caught early, the patients were likely not considered to have the disease because they lacked travel history to countries where malaria typically circulates, meaning treatment was delayed.

“This is why we alerted the medical people in Frankfurt, if you have odd cases presenting at your clinic, please also consider that there might be malaria around,” Dr Tinnemann said.

“There is this assumption that people who get sick with a nasty fever in places like Frankfurt and elsewhere that have not travelled cannot have malaria, and we don’t bother to investigate. That’s got to stop. That’s why these people die,” Joe Lines, Professor of Malaria Control and Vector Biology at the London School of Tropical Hygiene and Medicine, told The Telegraph.

Before the two cases in Schwanheim – both of which occurred at least 3 miles from the airport where the first malaria cases were reported – investigators were working on the hypothesis that just a single mosquito was responsible for the outbreak, but the new cases have cast doubt on that theory.

“We expect mosquitoes to live between one and three weeks on average,” said Dr Tinnemann.

“We had five cases in the beginning of July, then another in August - at that point, there was a good chance that potentially it could just be one bug. But now it seems at least there must be one other,” he said.

Frankfurt’s public health board have now shipped blood samples from all eight patients to a specialised lab in Antwerp, Belgium, where scientists can carry out DNA analysis to indicate if the infections came from one or multiple mosquitoes, and are awaiting results.

As temperatures warm, experts fear that several tropical mosquito-borne diseases – including malaria, dengue fever, Zika virus, and chikungunya could become established across Europe.

Earlier this month, a colony of Aedes aeypti mosquitoes – the bugs responsible for transmitting dengue and Zika virus – were found breeding in a residential area in East London for the first time.

Airfinity, the disease-monitoring company, said of the malaria outbreak in Frankfurt: “the risk to the wider public remains low but non-zero.”

“Continued vector surveillance, rapid diagnosis, and ready access to antimalarials are critical to prevent further severe outcomes.”

News.title: Global fund utilises AI to tackle malaria, TB, and HIV amid aid cuts
News.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to soften the blow from aid cuts, according to one of the world’s biggest development funds.

The Global Fund, which raises and invests billions of pounds to reduce the burden of HIV, tuberculosis (TB) and malaria globally says new AI-driven products like portable pregnancy scanners are helping to mitigate the funding gap.

“[We] have adapted pretty quickly to the changes in the funding environment; it has undoubtedly had negative impacts on health outcomes [...], but in some ways, the resilience of life-saving services has been remarkable,” Peter Sands, the executive director of the Global Fund, told The Telegraph.

The Global Fund is managing a $6 billion (£4.4bn) shortfall for the period 2026 to 2028 and has been forced to make difficult decisions to continue their work, it confirmed this week.

The gap comes as Western governments shift money from foreign aid to defence. The UK reduced its contribution to the fund by 15 per cent last year to £850 million, down from £1 billion.

But Mr Sands said investments in tools to tackle infectious diseases – including those driven by AI – are starting to pay off.

“Innovation is absolutely part of the answer when money is short. One of the few ways you can get to make the money go further is to have a better tool, a better way of doing things,” Mr Sands said.

News.title: Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players
News.content:
Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

News.title: Fiji declares national crisis as HIV epidemic escalates
News.content:
“The rollout has been slow and frustrating, and Fiji will pay for it in terms of lives lost,” said Prof Lisa Maher, an epidemiologist at the Kirby Institute in Sydney who is supporting Fiji’s response. “This is the only thing that will turn the epidemic around and stop people dying, and stop onward transmission of HIV to the general population.”

But the emergency declaration should provide political cover to introduce the needle and syringe programme, with a Cabinet subcommittee now created to remove barriers to action.

“The government is signalling that it is prepared to act in this particularly important and controversial area,” said Prof Maher. “It’s not coincidental that the draft bill [to legalise the distribution of needles and syringes for certain groups] now looks likely to go before parliament, after being blocked for 10 months… So it’s not just symbolic.”

Dr Jason Mitchell, head of Fiji’s HIV taskforce, added: “Since the government announced [the crisis], it has followed with some very rapid actions in progressing the needle and syringe programme. So that is being fast tracked through the necessary channels, and the government is determined to get that out in the next couple of weeks.

“We’ve gotten to the point where we really needed to take some really strong action,” he told The Telegraph. “This is the government realising that there have been challenges, and they need to step it up.”

It is hoped that the declaration will also turbocharge other elements of the response – for instance the scale-up of the post-exposure prophylaxis (Prep) scheme, which was introduced in May – as the virus gains a foothold in the broader population.

Although there has been a major focus on testing, treatment and education, UNAIDS still estimates that only 39 per cent of an estimated 9,100 people living with HIV in 2025 knew their positive status. Just 22 per cent were accessing antiretroviral treatment, and 117 people died in 2025, compared to 25 in 2021.

News.title: Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing
News.content:
There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

News.title: Banton shows his worth as England cruise to series victory against Sri Lanka
News.content:
A patchy Test team and a one-day international side learning on the job should not obscure the fact that under Harry Brook, England have built a formidable T20 outfit.

Missing a slew of first-choice players, they dispatched Sri Lanka with a game to spare and an emphatic show of their depth in the format, with Sonny Baker and Tom Banton – two men still finding their feet in the side – to the fore. England have now won 20 of the 23 completed T20s since Brook took over last year, and six matches in a row this summer. It is easily their best format and, as Liam Dawson said, they have “match-winners throughout” and plenty of “freak” performers.

In this six-wicket win, Baker’s one for 15 limited England’s target to a paltry 146, which Banton, a natural opener who is being recommissioned in the middle order, helped knock off with 47 balls remaining. “Tonight was a special performance, very clinical,” said Brook.

News.title: Interest rate increase ‘likely’, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Andrew Bailey has said that interest rates are likely to rise if the Middle East war rages on, warning inflation is now on course to hit 4pc.

The Bank of England opted to hold borrowing costs at 3.75pc on Thursday, the sixth time in a row it has left them unchanged.

However, the Governor said a “material” increase in energy prices since July would push up inflation to twice the Bank’s 2pc target.

He warned the outlook for inflation “continues to be on the upside” and criticised the “seeming loss of urgency to find solutions” to the war in Iran.

Oil prices are back above $100 a barrel and analysts expect average gas and electricity bills to rise above £2,000 this winter as the conflict continues.

Mr Bailey said: “So far, higher global energy costs have had a limited effect on price and wage setting in the UK.

“But the longer this volatility persists, the bigger the impact it will have on inflation, and the more likely it is we will need to raise Bank Rate to ensure that inflation falls back to our 2pc target.”

Investors expect the Bank to raise interest rates as soon as November, which has pushed average mortgage rates to their highest level in three years.

The average five-year fixed mortgage deal has risen to 5.87pc, according to Moneyfacts, which is the highest level since November 2023 and up from 4.95pc before the Iran war.

Thursday’s rate hold leaves the Bank out of step with central banks around the world after the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank voted to raise borrowing costs this month.

However, economists said there had been a change in tone from policymakers over the threat posed by energy prices and whether this would feed into the wider economy.

The Bank of England predicted that inflation would hit 4pc early next year, just as most workers are negotiating pay rises.

Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said: “It seems as though a majority of the MPC is on the cusp of wanting to tighten policy.”

In a warning on the impending pain facing households, Mr Bailey told the Chancellor that energy bills would rise by 24pc early next year under the Ofgem price cap.

This will push up annual average bills by £413 to £2,136, which the Governor blamed on the war in the Middle East.

The Governor is required to write a formal letter to the Chancellor every time inflation is more than a percentage point above its 2pc target.

Official data showed inflation rose to 3.1pc in August.

Mr Bailey said: “The energy price shock has been the most important factor driving recent short-term movements in inflation.”

Despite expectations of higher rates, the FTSE 100 rose on Thursday at its steepest pace since July, climbing more than 1pc, as the Bank of England eased the pressure on the UK bond market.

Policymakers also confirmed a Telegraph report that the Bank will stop selling the long-dated bonds it amassed during the financial crisis and lockdown.

The Bank will continue actively selling £20bn of government bonds per year until the rest of the stockpile is wound down to zero in 2034.

The announcement triggered a sharp fall in the cost of borrowing for the Treasury, with the yield on 30-year UK gilts falling at the fastest pace since May.

News.title: Next-generation antivenom fights India’s deadliest snakes
News.content:
The process to make antivenom has barely changed in a century: snakes are milked, their venom is injected into horses, and their antibodies are harvested to form the basis of the product. The resulting treatments are difficult to administer, can trigger severe side effects, and the quality varies from batch to batch.

“The big four snakes contribute to 70 per cent of poisonous bites [in India]… so 30 per cent of poisonous snakes are not covered, even to begin with,” said Dr Yogesh Jain, a public health physician in Chhattisgarh state and a member of The Global Snakebite Taskforce.

“But there are huge quality and efficacy issues even against these 70 per cent of bites. We’re relying on a 100-year-old technique of getting antivenoms, and at least 50,000 people are dying every year,” he told The Telegraph.

“There’s a real need for new technology. We don’t have a safe and appropriate antivenom for the largest majority of people in rural India.”

Now, scientists are hopeful that they have developed a potential alternative.

In the latest study, published last week, researchers showed that an experimental antivenom cocktail with five components protected mice against lethal doses of antivenom in Indian cobras, even when delayed by up to 20 minutes – a scenario that mimics the real-world lag between a bite and treatment.

“If you go 10 years back, people didn’t think you could make sufficiently simple products with new, modern biotechnology that could cover all these different snake venoms,” said Prof Andreas Laustsen-Kiel, head of the Section of Biologics Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark and co-author of the paper.

“People simply believed it was too complex, too expensive to manufacture, and so on… But the data we are gathering is convincing enough to say this is something that could make a huge dent in the lost lives and limbs snakebite causes every year.”

The antivenom itself was based on lab-made nanobodies – antibodies derived from a group of animals including camels, llamas and some species of shark. Scientists believe their structure means they could be a more potent, more precise, more temperature-stable alternative to man-made monoclonal antibodies – and cheaper to manufacture.

“The latest study builds on an earlier discovery of nanobodies that can protect across a broad spectrum of African snakes,” said Prof Nicholas Casewell, director of the Centre for Snakebite Research and Interventions at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, who has previously collaborated with Prof Laustsen-Kiel.

“In this paper they have iterated and demonstrated that a narrow number of nanobodies can protect against Indian cobras and king cobras. This demonstration brings the nanobody technology closer to market,” he added.

But that is likely still years away, depending on how much funding the researchers can attract. The next steps – a larger animal study, scaling up manufacture, and launching human trials – are expensive.

“If money was no issue, we could probably be testing in humans in 1.5 to three years from now,” said Prof Laustsen-Kiel. “But since money is a big issue, it is more likely that human trials won’t be able to start until 2.5 to four years from now.

“But I really think that this [study shows] there’s no doubt that biotech can deliver better antivenoms. The question is whether people are willing to fund it,” he said.

Sports.title: Coventry conned me into believing they’d survive.. they’ll go down for not signing some big, ugly b******s in summer
Sports.content:

COVENTRY impressed me so much over the summer — but after all their talk, I now feel like I’ve been lied to.

There was so much chat after their promotion about being pragmatic, adapting to opponents — and that meant I tipped them to stay up.



Their start, four Premier League games without a point, or even a goal, is desperately disappointing.

They have not backed up their talk from the summer, which made it sound like they were going to follow the lead of Sunderland, Brentford, Fulham or even the Watford teams I played in after promotion.



The recruitment was desperately poor and it has left manager Frank Lampard with a team every other manager would relish taking on.

You look at what Hull have done, or Sunderland last season, and that is the model to follow.



They both signed experience, but also some big, ugly b******* who are ready for the top-flight fight.

It is not about coming up from the Championship and impressing people, everything you do in that first season has to be all about surviving.

And, increasingly, teams have to do whatever it takes. There is no room for nostalgia, some need 13 or 14 new players.

When I was first promoted with Watford, at the start of the season there were four or five of us in the starting XI from the season before.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

By the end of the window, it was just me. That is the level of improvement needed.

What is most disappointing is it looks like Coventry have come up and decided that they’re going to play, we’re going to do this and that and have nice forwards.

The Premier League is horrible, you have to beat up other teams before you even think about earning the right to start playing.

It feels unfair to dig anyone specific out, but Matt Grimes encapsulates the problem. He’s a very good football player, legendary in the Championship.



But we’re now seeing the reason that people have never taken him in the Premier League.

He’s not as mobile as everybody else. It’s not disrespectful, just factual. That is across the entire Coventry squad.

They don’t have the pace or the power to compete with the rest of the league.

That is the biggest test, the speed of movement and thought everyone else has. You cannot step up and outplay these players, they are better than you. You must make it a fight.

A Brighton team without a number of key players steamrolled the Sky Blues at the weekend. I was on the end of some batterings with Watford, but against the big boys, like Manchester City.



Brighton, half-fit at that, is a different story — that is a problem. The spending decisions have been hard to work out.

Lampard’s missed opportunity

They’ve spent £22.5million on Carl Rushworth in goal, but there is no point having a mint keeper if no one in front of him can stop the shots.

Could they have got him on loan for another season, with a clause to buy him if they stay up? And then invested in those ahead of him properly?

Could Lampard not have tapped up his old club Chelsea to pick up some experienced bodies from their bomb squad?

Chelsea have countless players surplus to requirements. Surely Cov could have moved for someone like Tosin Adarabioyo or Axel Disasi.



When we came up with Watford, signings like Etienne Capoue raised the level for everyone and had us all on our toes.

I still remember the first training session with Capoue after he arrived from Tottenham, and it was eye-opening.

I went nine games without a goal at the start of that first Premier League season, having hit bucketloads in the Championship.

Runs like that get in your head, and the Coventry players would be lying if they were to say the fear of not ever picking up a win was not building in the back of their minds.

But part of the test is moving past that. After I scored my first, I felt like I was floating. They have to hold on to reaching that moment.



For now, I’m not too worried about Lampard. He has done so much for them, it would be foolish to make a change now. But I am disappointed — and all that could change quickly.

Under now-Barcelona manager Hansi Flick, the side fell to a shocking 2-1 loss to Japan in their opening match of the tournament.

A draw with Spain and a comfortable win over Costa Rica then proved only good enough for third place in the group, which saw them tumble out without a taste of knockout football for the second edition of the tournament in a row.



The fallout was felt across the country, with Flick being placed under heavy scrutiny for his tactical decisions during the competition.

And it was then that Watzke has admitted that he considered bringing in his former Borussia Dortmund colleague Tuchel.



Watzke told Sky Sports when asked whether he considered Tuchel for the job: “Well, not in the summer. But I did have the idea.

Flick managed to just about hold on to his role in the end, with the German FA resolving to stay with the boss for the 2024 Euros in Germany.

But he would not get that far, finally being sacked after an embarrassing 4-1 friendly loss to Japan in September 2023.

Sports.title: Prem must stop turning every goal into forensic investigation.. AI might be death of us but I’ll take it if it fixes VAR
Sports.content:
Next

LAST Sunday, the Premier League gave us another VAR controversy. Another goal that should not have stood. Another explanation afterwards.

Another reminder that football has somehow made getting the right decision more complicated by giving referees more information. Then came the League Cup, where VAR was absent.



Suddenly football looked quite capable of surviving without somebody in a room full of screens studying every camera angle before deciding what everyone else had already seen.

I saw Erling Haaland the following day — less than 24 hours after he had scored the controversial winner. He was, unsurprisingly, extremely pleased with the result. I doubt many Manchester United supporters were.



It’s left me pondering whether A.I. might be the answer? And yet I can’t help thinking it might be simpler to move good, old-fashioned human error from Stockley Park back to the pitch.

The extraordinary thing about the Manchester derby was not simply that VAR got it wrong. Referees get things wrong. That’s football.

The extraordinary thing was that the referee made a decision, VAR reviewed it, had every possible angle available, watched it again and still came to the wrong conclusion.

Pro Ref subsequently acknowledged the goal should not have stood, with Howard Webb describing the problem as “tunnel vision”.

The VAR team concentrated on whether Haaland was offside and failed properly to consider other players in an offside position.

I was in the room when Premier League clubs voted to retain VAR in 2024. I voted to retain it.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But that was not a vote of confidence. It was certainly not 20 clubs saying: “This is working brilliantly, please carry on”.

Frustrations ran deep. But there was also a recognition that simply throwing away the technology would create another set of problems. So, we voted to keep it, with significant improvements promised.

And, to be fair, some improvements have happened. Semi-automated offside has made the process quicker and there is more communication around decisions and work on training, consistency and transparency.

But none of that addresses the fundamental problem. The technology can tell you if a player is offside but it cannot stop the operator looking at the wrong thing. That is what happened in the Manchester derby.

What we wanted in that Premier League meeting was not faster VAR. We wanted better VAR. One wrong decision is infuriating for the biggest clubs but for a smaller club, it can be transformational.



Every point matters. It can mean a different position in the table and perhaps survival rather than relegation.

If a referee makes a mistake at full speed, you can at least understand it as part of the human nature of football.

It is much harder to swallow when somebody has had time to watch it again, slow it down, examine it and — and still gets it wrong. Which brings me to another question: Who is actually being hurt by VAR?

The dangers of using AI Chatbots Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots have become increasingly prevalent in our daily lives, assisting with everything from customer service to personal tasks. However, concerns about safety and privacy have arisen due to the extensive data these chatbots collect and process. Users may not always be aware of the information they are sharing, which can include sensitive personal details. One of the primary concerns is that conversations with AI chatbots are often stored and analysed to improve the service. This data can potentially be accessed by third parties, raising fears about unauthorised use and breaches of privacy. Additionally, the data might be used to create highly personalised profiles of users, which can then be exploited for targeted advertising or other purposes. Experts suggest several measures to mitigate these risks, such as being cautious about the information shared with chatbots and understanding the privacy policies of the services used. It is also recommended to regularly review and manage privacy settings and to be aware of the potential for data breaches. As AI technology continues to evolve, ongoing vigilance and updated regulations will be essential to ensure the safety and privacy of users.

At a shareholders’ meeting, I asked whether the league could provide a cumulative table of the negative VAR interventions affecting each club. The answer was no.

The League did not want to produce it because it could be construed as a league table and, if released to the media, potentially used to recreate the actual table.



I don’t really understand that. I wasn’t asking for a new league table. Just a simple question: Who is actually being helped by VAR and who is being hurt by it?

Why shouldn’t clubs be able to see if mistakes are falling evenly across the league? I am not suggesting there is a conspiracy against smaller clubs nor anyone deliberately favours big ones.

But if the league is confident VAR errors are simply random human mistakes, surely transparency can only help demonstrate that.

Transparency should not be confused with conspiracy. The problem with VAR is we have not removed human error from football.

We have moved it from the pitch to a room full of screens. Perhaps the answer is not more VAR — perhaps it is less.



Leave more decisions to referees on the pitch. Intervene when there is an obvious error but stop turning every goal and tackle into a forensic investigation.

And then there is A.I, which we are told will be the death of us all.

Frankly, if it can sort out VAR first, I’ll take my chances.

At least there would be no VAR official having a bad day. Though A.I will not solve everything.

If the laws are subjective, artificial intelligence will not suddenly make them mathematical.

Football is a human game. Perhaps we should stop trying to make it something else.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The League Cup gives us a great comparison. Decisions are made, mistakes happen, supporters celebrate, supporters complain, and everyone goes home.

Nobody pretends it is perfect. But perhaps perfection is the wrong target.

FOR the first time in 14 years, Millwall and West Ham will clash on the football pitch.

This Saturday, English football is graced by the 100th Dockers’ Derby that sees the Lions of South London take on the Irons of East London.



It is one of the most bitter rivalries in all of football, let alone in England, dating back to the 19th century.

The Met Police are set to deploy a whopping 400 officers across South East London as supporters of both sides descend on The Den, which will be the crucible in which the game is played.



The last time these two sides met saw Saturday’s visitors emerge with a 2-1 win at their old home, Upton Park, in the Championship.

Goals from Carlton Cole and Winston Reid sealed a famous win even despite Kevin Nolan’s sending off after just nine minutes for a two-footed challenge.

Millwall‘s Liam Trotter scored an equaliser before Reid smashed home a volley into an empty net, controversially after David Forde was taken out and left sprawled on the floor after punching a cross away.

Some remarkable names who are known to fans across the country ended up on the pitch that day.

Sports.title: York Valkyrie win at Leeds to book Women's Super League Grand Final vs Wigan
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player York Valkyrie travelled to Leeds Rhinos and posted a superb victory to progress to this year's Women's Super League Grand Final York Valkyrie travelled to Leeds Rhinos and posted a superb victory to progress to this year's Women's Super League Grand Final

York Valkyrie are through to the 2026 Women's Super League Grand Final against Wigan Warriors following a superb 12-0 semi-final away victory over Leeds Rhinos.

York will now face defending champions Wigan in the Grand Final at the Brick Community Stadium on Sunday September 27 (5.30pm kick-off), live on Sky Sports.

York, who were beaten 38-16 by Leeds on August 8, and 44-0 by Wigan a week later on August 15, have totally turned fortunes around since, defeating Leeds at home, St Helens away and Wigan at home before sealing semi-final success.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

The opening 21 minutes proved scoreless at Headingley in a tight contest, before York's Liv Wood twisted, turned and wrestled over to ground the ball for a try in the 22nd minute. Tara Jane Stanley converted for the full haul.

As the first half drew to a close and with Leeds camped on the York try-line on the verge of a try, a grubber-kick on the last by Leeds' Ruby Walker proved a poor one and allowed Stanley to gather and run clear.

Instead, York were next to add points as Stanley struck a penalty superbly from distance for a lead of 8-0 three minutes from the end of the half.

Eight minutes into the second half, Stanley accelerated forward and forced her way over for York's second try and clear daylight on the scoreboard - but the Video Ref then proved via replays she lost control in the act of scoring to rule it out.

Buoyed by their reprieve, Leeds came back attacking hard at York, but Valkyrie defended superbly to keep their two-score lead intact.

On the hour mark, Leeds' Georgia Elliston powered her way over under the sticks for a try, but again the score was ruled out by the Video Ref, who ruled obstruction.

York then wrapped up victory through Adaoha Akwiwu's try as she burst through off a Stanley short-ball pass for a 12-0 advantage.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

With six minutes remaining, Leeds' Ebony Stead appeared to charge over for a try out wide to give Rhinos brief hope, but for a third time on the night the Video Ref ruled out a score, as replays proved Stead had lost control of the ball while going over.

The contest ended on a sour note for York too, with the news Stanley - their standout performer on the night - had failed a Head Injury Assessment (HIA), ruling her out of the Grand Final.

York proved the better side defensively and in attack on the day vs Leeds

Pryce: Nobody gave us a chance - we've made it against all odds

York Valkyrie head coach Leon Pryce to Sky Sports:

"This is unbelievable. Nobody gave us a chance.

"Everyone had written us off, and last week they were saying it was going to be another Saints vs Leeds game after Saints won here.

"We read the comments and used that as fuel. I don't think we got the respect we deserved, but they've been unbelievable.

"To come to Leeds in a semi-final against a really good squad and keep them to zero just shows.

"It was going to be about grit, toughness and determination.

"Against all odds we've got there and I couldn't be more proud.

"I've been proud of them all season, but the last four or five weeks we've really turned a corner and we don't want the season to end."

Wigan trio make up shortlist for 2026 Woman of Steel

Wigan Warriors will dominate the 2026 Woman of Steel awards, with three players from the reigning Women's Super League champions shortlisted for the competition's most prestigious individual honour.

Jenna Foubister, Eva Hunter and Megan Williams have all been named on the three-player shortlist ahead of Rugby League Awards Night in Manchester, which will take place on the evening of Tuesday September 29.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Foubister's nomination comes after another influential season at the heart of Wigan's attack in 2026. The 19-year-old half-back contributed a return of nine tries in 18 appearances across all competitions and has continued to establish herself as one of the leading playmakers in the women's game. Foubister also produced a Player of the Match performance in the Women's Challenge Cup Final at Wembley Stadium, creating two tries and providing three line-break assists as the Warriors lifted the trophy for a second time.

Reigning Woman of Steel Hunter has enjoyed another prolific campaign under Denis Betts, crossing for 23 tries in all competitions. The dynamic second-rower has continued to showcase her devastating pace, powerful ball-carrying and defensive intensity throughout the season, while also writing her name into the history books by becoming the first woman to score four tries in a Challenge Cup Final at Wembley Stadium.

Williams' place on the Woman of Steel shortlist follows a remarkable first two seasons with the Cherry & White, having quickly established herself as one of the competition's most consistent forwards. Since joining the club ahead of the 2025 campaign from St Helens, the England Knights international has become a key figure in Betts' side. The loose forward has scored four tries since the competition split into the Super Four phase, helping Wigan maintain their push for another historic season.

Watch the Women's Super League Grand Final between Wigan Warriors and York Valkyrie live on Sky Sports on Sunday September 27, with kick-off at 5.30pm.

Sports.title: No charges against Carse after police close alleged assault investigation
Sports.content:
Derbyshire Police have ended their investigation into an alleged assault incident which involved England and Durham cricketer Brydon Carse; Carse, who has played for Durham in the County Championship during the investigation over the last month, will not face any charges

Brydon Carse: No charges against England cricketer after police close investigation into alleged assault at nightclub

Brydon Carse will not face any charges after an investigation

Brydon Carse will not face any charges after Derbyshire Police closed their investigation into an alleged assault following an incident involving the England cricketer at a nightclub in Derby.

Last month, Carse was handcuffed outside a nightclub in Derby and missed the second and third Tests of England's series against Pakistan.

The 31-year-old was celebrating with Durham players after their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship and was also seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background.

In a statement, Derbyshire Police said: "An investigation into reports of an assault in Derby city centre has been closed.

"Officers attended Molly Malones in the Wardwick, Derby, in the early hours of Sunday 23 August. A man was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly and was then de-arrested after his details were taken by officers."

Subsequent enquiries were made pursuing the allegations of an assault but, after the alleged victim was identified and spoken to, no further action was taken, police said.

The matter is now in the hands of the independent Cricket Regulator, which will assess if Carse has a disciplinary issue to answer to relating to his conduct.

Sky Sports News has contacted the England and Wales Cricket Board for comment.

Image: Brydon Carse missed the second and third Tests against Pakistan following the incident

Carse has continued playing for Durham since the episode took place, helping his side win the Division Two title of the Rothesay County Championship, but he has been overlooked by England.

He was immediately removed from the squad ahead of the second Test against Pakistan, then left out of the final match too. While officially considered available for selection for the ongoing white-ball series against Sri Lanka, he was left on the sidelines once again.

Speaking earlier this week, England's limited-overs head coach Brendon McCullum called for his side to be mindful of their off-field responsibilities and added: "I've spoken to Carsey a lot and it's the same message - you need to make good decisions off the field that allow you to be able to be the best version of yourself.

"As far as Carsey is concerned, it's a good chance for him now to get his house in order and then push for selection for the next opportunity that arises."

Image: Since making his international Test debut in October 2024, Brydon Carse has been England's wicket taker with 58 wickets to his name, including 22 in last winter's Ashes (PA Images)

Test captain Joe Root also had his say ahead of the Lord's Test when he described himself as "hacked off" by the growing list of alcohol-related incidents involving England players.

On Carse, he said: "I don't think I'm speaking out of turn in saying he's very upset, very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself."

Sports.title: Gerard surges to take clubhouse lead, as McIlroy impresses at Wentworth
Sports.content:
Ryan Gerard leapfrogged Adam Scott and Filippo Celli to take a two-shot lead at the halfway stage of the BMW PGA Championship, as Rory McIlroy impressed on day two to finish four shots off the lead.

Scott and Celli had climbed to take a share of the clubhouse lead midway through the second round at 10 under par, but Gerard surged in the afternoon, posting a flawless bogey-free seven-under 65 to finish his day at 12 under.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyrrell Hatton holed out from a bunker and Alex Fitzpatrick chipped in over water to make the cut on the last hole of the day

Aaron Rai, who co-led coming into Friday's round, finished tied with Manuel Elvira for fourth, while his playing partners, McIlroy and Ryan Fox, trailed them by one shot, sharing sixth place with five other players at eight under par.

Some big names missed the cut on Friday at Wentworth, including European Ryder Cup stars Jon Rahm and Tommy Fleetwood, who finished at three over on day two.

The Spaniard endured a torrid two days at Wentworth, going 11 over par through 36 holes, to plummet to the worst 36-hole score of his career, and to last place on the leaderboard.

Tyrrell Hatton and Matt Fitzpatrick had at times been in danger of missing the cut too on Friday, but both produced remarkable finishes, with each chipping in on the 18th, to finish at four under par.

Image: It was a tough day for Jon Rahm who slumped to finish eleven over through 36 holes

Hatton would make an eagle with his chip from the greenside bunker, while Fitzpatrick clipped a wedge over the stream on the 18th to make birdie.

Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed was, meanwhile, forced to withdraw due to injury on the ninth hole after the American had also endured a poor start to his front nine, going eight over par through nine holes.

In windy conditions at Wentworth, Gerard struggled to keep his ball on the fairway with his driver, but he was superb with his approach play, drilling a brilliant long iron into the green on the fourth to set himself up for birdie, before following up with another on the eighth.

Back-to-back birdies on 12 and 13 would see him go within one shot of Scott and Celli, and he leapfrogged both players with an eagle on the par-five 17th, thanks to another long iron out of the rough.

Gerard admitted he had tried to stay patient all day, and it paid off, with the 27-year-old wrapping up his round with a birdie on the 18th.

"I don't know if I was feeling an eagle, birdie finish, but I stayed patient all day," Gerard said.

"You know when you get to the last couple holes at Wentworth here, they are gettable. There's also trouble lurking, so you have to be careful.

"I just felt like we were putting the ball in the right spots all day. Good things happen when you stick to the plan and execute shots."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Robert MacIntyre sensationally chipped in for an eagle on the 15th on Friday

Scott was once again in flying form at Wentworth, notably carding four straight birdies on holes 14 through 17.

It came after the 2013 Masters champion, who began his round on the ninth, got off to a slow start, going one over through his opening four holes, but he revealed that a mid-round putting adjustment helped him find his rhythm.

"Over the first couple of holes, my rhythm was a little out," the Australian said. "I made an adjustment on the fifth green, and it went in, so I ran with that for the rest of the day.

"Sometimes you just have to find that one little thing, and I'm glad I made that adjustment early. Kind of helps the rest of the game; when you feel like the putter is good, you free up the rest of the game."

McIlroy improves after faltering late in first round

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy enjoyed a much improved day at Wentworth, going eight under par through 36 holes

After admitting he "stumbled" towards the end of his first round, McIlroy produced a much improved performance in front of huge crowds of fans, who had arrived to see the career Grand Slam winner perform at Wentworth on Friday.

The Masters champion again got off to a flying start, going four under through five, and had the crowd roaring on the par-three second when he chipped in from off the green for birdie.

A missed fairway on the eighth would prove costly, but he hit back with birdies on 11 and 14, before overshooting an approach on the 16th to give another shot back to the course. He ended his round with a flourish, making back-to-back birdies on holes 17 and 18.

"I'm playing a bit better today than I did yesterday and hit a lot more fairways," he said. "Felt like I drove the ball better. Gave myself a few more chances.

"I didn't feel like I was scrambling my way around most of the day today. Solid round."

Sports.title: Gabriel edging closer to Man Utd exit as Barca and Real talks advance
Sports.content:
Barcelona and Real Madrid are in transfer talks to sign Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel.

The 15-year-old and his family are currently in Barcelona, where discussions with the Catalan club and their LaLiga rivals are advancing.



PSG and Bayern Munich also remain interested in his signature.

Gabriel and his team lodged a request earlier this week to leave United.

The club's leadership have been hopeful they can persuade the young star to stay at the club as he is contracted until the end of the season, but it now looks increasingly likely he will move away from Old Trafford.

Gabriel and his family put in a formal request to be de-registered after the UEFA Youth League tie against Sabah last Thursday - a game United won 5-0 with Gabriel scoring a hat-trick.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Khan updates Sky Sports on Gabriel's decision to leave Manchester United

Gabriel, who was not named in any of England's youth squads announced on Friday despite representing England most recently at U17 level, has not trained with United since then.

There is a belief - owing to a precedent due to a FIFA loophole - that Gabriel could leave United for a club in Europe once he turns 16 [on October 6] if he obtains a European passport that he could get through either of his parents.

Image: Manchester United celebrate Gabriel's opener in the FA Youth Cup semi-final

However, any move for Gabriel would be subject to FIFA approval.

United head coach Michael Carrick was asked about Gabriel on Friday and reiterated his view that the matter needed to be handled carefully.

"I think he's a young boy, JJ, and I think it's important that we certainly don't play anything out here," he said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick has urged care in the handling of Gabriel, after the 15-year-old requested to leave the club

"I think the exposure and the scrutiny and everything, you've got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything, so the situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's okay is the important thing."

Merson: Massive blow if Gabriel leaves

Sky Sports' Paul Merson:

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Paul Merson says teenage sensations Max Dowman and Gabriel need to be patient as they look to build their careers

"First of all, he's an unbelievable talent. The problem now is with the lad and probably his agents and his family - I don't know him so I'm only thinking from the outside.

"When you're watching Max Dowman at Arsenal and Rio Ngumoha getting given a chance at Liverpool and doing very well, he's probably thinking, 'I should be playing at Man Utd now as well'.

"This is the problem you're going to have with the kids of this day and age. They're so talented that they want to play straight away. When I was playing, it was unheard of at 16.

"It'll be a massive blow for Man Utd. Believe me, this kid is an unbelievable talent. They'll have every club in the world wanting him."

Sports.title: Will Celtic ease the pressure or Rangers narrow the gap?
Sports.content:
Will Derek McInnes complete the double against Celtic, or can Martin O'Neill recover from a nightmare week to move eight points clear of Rangers?

The Old Firm sides meet in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, seven days after the Ibrox side laid down a marker with an emphatic League Cup win.

While McInnes appears to have weathered an early storm at Rangers, O'Neill is looking for solutions after Celtic followed up that 3-0 defeat with a 3-1 loss to Ferencvaros in the Europa League.

Only Celtic fans will be inside Parkhead at the order of the authorities amid a ticket allocation spat between the two Glasgow giants.

We look at some of the talking points ahead of what is sure to be another fascinating encounter...

Is pressure mounting on O'Neill?

It is amazing how quickly things can change in football.

Just a few months ago, O'Neill was at peak legendary Celtic status after saving their season to deliver a league and cup double.

They then capitulated against LASK and crashed out of the Champions League, but a winning domestic start kept the pressure off.

Image: Celtic have suffered back-to-back defeats

However, the League Cup defeat to Rangers, followed by their Europa League loss to Ferencvaros means Sunday could be seen as a must-win for the veteran boss - even if the 74-year-old does not think so.

Celtic are guaranteed to go into the international break top of the Scottish Premiership, but few Celtic fans would accept back-to-back defeats to their fiercest rivals. Especially when they have dominated domestically for so long.

O'Neill will be desperately seeking solutions ahead of Sunday's game after admitting their confidence has taken a hit.

Is McInnes out the woods?

While the pressure is mounting at Parkhead, it appears to be easing at Ibrox after a turbulent start for McInnes.

Failure to secure European football and a slow start domestically had many wondering if he was the right manager to deliver silverware.

Image: Rangers are looking for their fifth straight win

But then the results started to come, and a tactical masterclass against Celtic to reach the League Cup semi-finals has switched the momentum.

The former Rangers midfielder backed himself to bring success to the club and victory on Sunday would put them just two points behind Celtic in the Scottish Premiership.

But defeat would leave them eight points in arrears after just seven games. If that happens, the scrutiny would no doubt return.

Big selection issues for Celtic

Image: It was a tough night for Celtic against Ferencvaros

It is not just a selection headache, but a dizzying migraine facing O'Neill - with five key positions to ponder before Sunday's showdown.

You can only confidently predict six of his starting XI: captain Callum McGregor, talismanic midfielder Benjamin Nygren, top scorer Camilo Duran, fans' favourite Kieran Tierney, reliable defender Cameron Carter-Vickers and academy graduate Colby Donovan.

GK: Goalkeeper Sam Johnstone was less than convincing on his Old Firm debut last weekend and was replaced by previous No 1 Viljami Sinisalo against Ferencvaros on Thursday.

LCB: Liam Scales and Auston Trusty regularly trade places at left centre-back, but the former has started the last two matches in that position.

Image: Celtic's Liam Scales cleared a shot off the line at Ibrox but scored an own goal against the Hungarians

CM: Captain McGregor was left exposed as a solo sitting midfield player at Ibrox so O'Neill might be tempted to bring in Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain for Mika Baur to provide additional protection. He must weigh-up whether he sticks with one six and two eights or switches to two sixes and one 10.

RW: Haissem Hassan has impressed since signing from Real Oviedo this summer but was left out of the starting XI last Sunday. The Egyptian must surely be in contention - especially if Rangers are expected to defend three-vs-three at the back.

Image: Callum McGregor believes Sunday's game is the 'ultimate test' after a tough week

ST: Club-record signing Kasper Hogh has scored in just one of his seven matches for Celtic so far. He was left on the bench against Ferencvaros to allow Duran to operate in his more natural No 9 position and may find it difficult to dislodge the Colombian from there. If that were to be the case, it is a toss-up between James Forrest and Sebastian Tounekti for the left-wing berth.

Will Rangers stick or twist at Parkhead?

Image: Will Derek McInnes make changes for the Old Firm rematch?

McInnes got his game plan spot on at Ibrox, and Celtic could not live with his team.

He used left-back James Penrice as an auxiliary midfielder to flood the middle of the pitch - allowing Rangers to press Celtic man for man.

Djeidi Gassama and Min-Su Kim provided width and energy as wing-backs with Dujon Sterling, Emmanuel Fernandez and Olwethu Makhanya defending three-vs-three against Celtic's front line.

It was a bold decision that paid dividends as Celtic folded under the pressure.

Dan Neil snatched the starring role of midfield general from his Celtic counterpart McGregor, who was left isolated without a defensive-minded midfield partner.

Image: Dan Neil netted a double against Celtic as Rangers reached the League Cup semi finals

The former Sunderland man would probably have still been named player of the match even if he had not netted two famous derby goals.

But Celtic Park will be a different test, especially with no away fans.

McInnes opted for two strikers last Sunday, but he might plump for an extra body in the heart of midfield.

If he does switch, will it be Ryan Naderi or Kevin Kelsy in that No 9 role?

Image: Kevin Kelsy scored his first Rangers goal against Celtic

Kelsy scored his first Rangers goal last weekend and was a constant threat, Naderi provided the assist but is a doubt for Sunday's showdown with an ankle problem.

He also has the option of Bojan Miovski, a player who knows the intensity of playing at Celtic Park from his days with Aberdeen.

If McInnes gets it right, he will be the first manager since Walter Smith in 1991 to win his first two Old Firm games in charge.

What the managers said

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic manager Martin O'Neill is not too concerned about their form ahead of Sunday's Old Firm clash with Rangers, live on Sky Sports

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill:

"We're far from rock bottom.

"We're still in the lead and if we could win this, we can extend the lead and if we don't, even by the international break, we're still going to be in front.

"We're going to try and put that right if we can. But I know the last time we had an international break was in March time and we played very poorly against Dundee United.

"So that was, if you can call it a wake-up call or a moment of quiet reflection or whatever the case may be. We turned it round. The players are capable of turning it round.

"It's a big game, whether it's played in September or March time.

"We need to be up for the game. Do we need to win the game? It would be nice to win it, it wouldn't be great if we lost.

"That would be three on the trot. Psychologically, it would be a blow. But we need to be up for it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rangers manager Derek McInnes insists there will be no complacency from his players against Celtic on Sunday, live on Sky, despite last weekend's Old Firm win

Rangers boss Derek McInnes:

"Just because you win the game doesn't mean it always says you've got the tactics right and, equally, when you lose a game, it doesn't mean it says you've got them wrong.

"I think sometimes tactics can get a wee bit overplayed. I do think you normally win games during the individual moments and the performance of players being really high and really strong.

"We look to do something similar in terms of our approach. We want to make sure the aggression's there, the confidence is there to play.

"The energy that we displayed last week, these are all the things that are more important than tactics.

"Hopefully the players go into the game and onto the pitch with that message loud and clear that a big performance is required.

"You don't win at Celtic Park unless everybody plays well. We've got to try and bring something similar and look for those improvements again.

"Once the ball rolls, it's a game of football that we need to concentrate on the detail, in and out of possession, what we're looking to try and do."
