14m ago 15.44 EDT 44 min: Welbeck chases after a ball down the left. Ajer gives him a little tug on the shoulder from behind, and it’s surely a free kick and a booking, but the referee waves play on. Welbeck can’t believe it. Share

16m ago 15.43 EDT 42 min: Kelleher claims Henderson’s corner without fuss. The MacPhee Effect yet to kick in with Chelsea. Brentford counter quickly, and Lewis-Potter tries to steer a shot into the top right from his position on the left. Easy for Martinez. Share

17m ago 15.42 EDT 41 min: Chavarria turns on the jets to make off down the left. He cuts back for Rogers, in space just inside the box. Rogers hooks a fierce shot towards the right-hand side of the goal. Kelleher is going the correct way, but the ball pings off Schuster and out to the left of goal for a corner instead. Share

18m ago 15.40 EDT 39 min: Lewis-Potter bustles his way in from the left and lays off to Damsgaard. He’s hoping for the return down the inside-left channel, but instead of being released into the box, watches in irritation as Damsgaard lashes a wild shot over the bar. To be fair to Damsgaard, he was getting the Big Enthuse from the crowd. Share

22m ago 15.37 EDT 37 min: A bit of space for Yarmoliuk, just to the right of the Chelsea D. He gets Brentford’s first effort on target, but it’s a scuff towards the bottom left, and an easy job for Martinez to gather. Share

22m ago 15.36 EDT 36 min: Chavarria loops long down the left. Rogers, his back to goal, 50 yards out, splits the Brentford defence with an outrageous backheel down the channel, releasing Welbeck … but the flag goes up correctly for offside. A shame for aesthetes everywhere, because that could have been one of the all-time assists. Share

25m ago 15.33 EDT 33 min: It’s Schade versus Fofana again down the left, and this time the defender is forced to clank out for a throw. Another opportunity for Kayode to send his dangerous long throw into the mixer … View image in fullscreen Chelsea's Wesley Fofana. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at 15.48 EDT

26m ago 15.33 EDT 32 min: Keith Andrews certainly isn’t happy, and he’s now on the touchline offering his charges beneficial advice. Share

27m ago 15.31 EDT 30 min: Rogers floats a weak free kick straight into Kelleher’s arms. The steam-bothered status of Austin MacPhee’s hair not captured on camera this time. Share

29m ago 15.30 EDT 29 min: … but might it take off here? Damsgaard and Janelt take turns in having a nibble at Palmer, shielding the ball to the right of the Brentford D. A free kick in a dangerous position. It was right on the line … or inches outside of it, anyway. VAR double-checks for a spot kick, but free kick it is. Share

30m ago 15.28 EDT 27 min: Rogers wins a corner down the right … which comes to nothing. This game’s yet to take off. Share

31m ago 15.28 EDT 25 min: Kayode throws back to his keeper from the right touchline. Kelleher takes his eye off the ball, and lets it roll under his foot. It’s heading in, but Kelleher strolls back before hooking off the line. The calmest man in the stadium! Memories of poor old Peter Enckelman … but unlike the erstwhile Villa keeper, Kelleher gets away with a big one. Share

34m ago 15.25 EDT 24 min: The last couple of minutes have been better from Brentford, even if Martinez still hasn’t had work to do. Share

35m ago 15.23 EDT 23 min: … nothing much happens, Damsgaard unable to beat the first man. However the ball flies out to the left, and it’s another chance for Kayode to fling long. Which he does, and the ball drops to Lewis-Potter, who has a little bit of time to control and shoot, but only manages to blooter into the nearest defender. Not a clean contact. Share

36m ago 15.22 EDT 22 min: Damsgaard delivers, Welbeck clears. But Brentford come again, Ajer hooking artfully down the left for Schade to chase. The striker wins another corner, from which … Share

37m ago 15.21 EDT 21 min: Anthony is clipped by Chavarria out on the right. Before the free kick can be taken, Schade literally picks Barco up and throws him to the ground. It’s more comical than sinister. Then the ball’s sent into the mixer, and Henderson is forced to head behind for Brentford’s first corner of the evening. Share

39m ago 15.20 EDT 19 min: All of Brentford’s attacking ambition has been down the left so far. Lewis-Potter, Janelt and Schade paint some pretty triangles, but don’t really get anywhere. View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer of Chelsea is challenged by Kevin Schade and Kristoffer Ajer of Brentford. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.22 EDT

41m ago 15.18 EDT 17 min: Barco rolls a clever pass down the inside-left and nearly releases Rogers, but Kayode is on point to shepherd the ball out for a goal kick. Both attacks not quite clicking; the defences on top. Who’d have expected that? Share

42m ago 15.16 EDT 16 min: Lewis-Potter obviously fancies this ball down the left. Another long attempt to find a team-mate. Damsgaard chases after it, and this time Fofana’s nowhere to be seen, but there’s too much on the pass and it sails harmlessly out for a goal kick. Martinez has had nothing to do as of yet. Share

44m ago 15.15 EDT 15 min: Lewis-Potter looks long for Schade down the left again, but at the moment Fofana has that flank locked up. Share

45m ago 15.14 EDT 13 min: Chavarria wins a corner down the left. Henderson takes, keeping well clear of the nearby advertising boards. Fool me once, etc. The corner’s no use, but the panto boos are as loud as ever. Chelsea will be happy enough with their start. Share

46m ago 15.13 EDT 11 min: A free kick for Chelsea out on the right. Neto takes, and floats a dismal ball into the box. It drops like a feather into Kelleher’s arms. On the touchline, steam pours out of Austin MacPhee’s ears, the Chelsea set-piece guru’s flowing locks oscillating gently in the resulting breeze. View image in fullscreen Pedro Neto of Chelsea takes a shot on goal. Photograph: Anthony Hanc/Wired Photos/Shutterstock Share Updated at 15.20 EDT

48m ago 15.10 EDT 10 min: Lewis-Potter makes a hash of dealing with Chavarria’s left-wing cross, and the ball breaks to Neto, who peals a shot goalwards from a tight angle on the right. Kelleher is behind it all the way and parries with a strong hand. Chelsea on top in these early exchanges. Share

50m ago 15.08 EDT 8 min: Palmer dribbles into the Brentford box down the middle, and is gently tugged back by Janelt. No foul. Then Schade tries to make good up the left touchline, only to be eased off the ball by Neto and into the hoardings. No problem there either. The referee in a laissez-faire mood early doors. Share

52m ago 15.07 EDT 6 min: Some booing, as you’d expect, a smatter for the returning Henderson but most for poor Barco, who has been getting it in the neck all season for his post World Cup semi-final antics. Pantomime season soon! Share

53m ago 15.05 EDT 4 min: The first chance for Kayode to throw in long from the right. Whee! Thiago gets in Martinez’s way, but Rogers intercepts before the striker can get to the dropping ball and clears. “If Brentford are, as their fans like to remind others, just a ‘bus stop in Hounslow’, then it’s surely wise to have their ground located beside a cemetery, given most people’s experience with London buses. As for Chelsea? They’re the Pensioners. They’re hardly going to play beside a maternity hospital, now are they?” Justin Kavanagh answering Peter Oh’s pre-match query, ladies and gentlemen. He’s here all week. Try the Fuller’s. Share

1h ago 15.03 EDT 2 min: Schade advances menacingly down the left, chasing after a long ball by Lewis-Potter. He enters the box ahead of Fofana, but the Chelsea defender does magnificently well to catch up, take over possession, and brush Schade off the ball. Schade claims for a penalty, but not with any real conviction. We play on. It was a fine challenge. Share

1h ago 15.01 EDT Chelsea get the ball rolling at the Gtech. More accurately, Palmer sends it sailing directly into touch, rugby-style, down the right. A wonderful few-Friday-night-pints-in atmosphere. “If Brentford have no defence at centre back, do Chelsea have a defence anywhere?” wonders Richard Hirst. Share

1h ago 14.58 EDT The teams are out! Brentford wear their new red and white striped shirts with honey and black collars. They’ll be wearing those for two seasons, so hats off to them for maintaining that fan-friendly convention. Chelsea meanwhile give a competitive debut to their second-choice black tops which, the promotional copy insists, are a celebration of the “Italian Renaissance … of their transformative 1990s era”. A period during which their change shirts were, if memory serves, usually either yellow, white or that grey-and-orange Coors monstrosity. There was once an advert in Viz for vegetarian sausages made from 100 percent meat. The tagline was something along the lines of: we don’t know how they’re vegetarian, they just are. Well, that. Anyway, I digress. We’ll be off in a couple of minutes. Buckle in! Share

1h ago 14.40 EDT Pre-match postbag. “To double down on the introductory theme, every bookie quoting a price on there being at least seven goals in the match has that as more likely than a 0-0. Seven!” – David Howell “I don’t usually set much store by xG, but tonight’s game features a contrast in set-piece efficiency. Brentford have generated 2.34 xG from set pieces (second in the league) but managed just one actual goal. On the other hand, Chelsea have created a much lower 1.5 xG, but turned it into four goals (first in the league). Let’s see if the data catches up with either team tonight” – Andrew Goudie “Brentford have no defence at centre-back. Offensively, Brentford have to be on the front foot, around Chelsea’s box like a swarm of Bees” – AnhTuan Nguyen Huynh “Not being familiar with London I was curious about how long it takes to get from Stamford Bridge to the Brentford Community Stadium. A popular map app tells me that it’s only a 30-minute drive, or two-hour walk. I couldn’t help but notice that both stadiums are adjacent to cemeteries. Is this intriguing juxtaposition just coincidence or could there be more to it? Efficiencies in hiring groundskeeping staff? Season tickets for eternity?” – Peter Oh Share Updated at 14.43 EDT

2h ago 14.25 EDT Both teams have the chance to go third with a win tonight. A draw would nudge both up one spot … for 19 hours or so at least, when the likes of Brighton, Everton, Ipswich, Newcastle and Hull conclude their Saturday 3pm shenanigans. Share Updated at 14.57 EDT

2h ago 14.17 EDT As Alonso departs, the Sky microphone is passed, relay-baton style, to Keith Andrews of Brentford, who is first asked about Mamadou Sangaré. “You’ve obviously done a bit of preparation ready for him starting! … he’s done brilliantly, settled in so well … it isn’t easy in this league … but [Yehor Yarmolyuk] has been excellent, [Vitaly Janelt] has been excellent, we’ve got other midfielders … I’ve no doubt Mamadou will feature heavily tonight … we’re in a decent rhythm … I’ve no doubt [Igor Thiago’s first Premier League goal of the season] is coming, hopefully it’s tonight.” Share

2h ago 14.10 EDT Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso ambles out of the tunnel and has a pitchside word with Sky Sports. “We always try to assess the whole squad … we have a tough game for sure … the goal is always to have the most competitive team to play and I think we have one … we are prepared for tonight … we have not had enough continuity and stability in [central midfield] … having [Jordan Henderson] back is so important … he helps a lot of the players around … [defence] is fundamental … we need to improve in that part … to be solid … more efficient … that will come … still early days to work on some things … we are confident that we will get there.” He also reports that his missing captain Reece James has “a little injury in the hamstring”. Share

2h ago 13.57 EDT Brentford make two changes to the side sent out to face Bournemouth last weekend. Mikkel Damsgaard and Michael Kayode take the places of Aaron Hickery and Mamadou Sangaré, who are on the bench tonight. Chelsea make five changes following the draw with Hull City. Jordan Henderson makes his first appearance for the Blues on his old stomping ground, while Danny Welbeck, Valentín Barco and Pep Chavarría make their full Premier League debuts. Maxence Lacroix is also in. Roméo Lavia and Malo Gusto drop to the bench, while João Pedro, Jorrel Hato and Reece James sit this one out altogether. View image in fullscreen Brentford fans show their support before the match. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty Images Share Updated at 15.06 EDT

Sports.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold recalled by England but with a warning from Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has told Trent Alexander-Arnold he must bring defensive solidity to the England squad after giving him a surprise recall for the upcoming Nations League matches.

The head coach has selected the Real Madrid right-back only once before – for the games against Andorra and Senegal in June last year. Tuchel made headlines when he did so by urging Alexander-Arnold to focus on the defensive side of his game or risk a slip that could undermine the team’s World Cup campaign.

Tuchel used him as a 64th-minute substitute against Andorra and Alexander-Arnold was out of the picture by the time England went to North America for the tournament. He is now back, despite starting only three of Madrid’s seven matches this season and largely going under the radar with his performances. Tuchel’s message to him has not changed.

“He has to, it’s necessary,” Tuchel said when asked whether Alexander-Arnold offered enough defensively. “My conviction is that he will but he has no choice.”

Tuchel continues to see Alexander-Arnold, who is famed for the range of his passing, as a right-back rather than a midfielder. The head coach has previously said he has Tino Livramento and Jarell Quansah ahead of Alexander-Arnold in the right-back pecking order. He has named both of them in the squad for the games against Spain (home), Czechia (home and away) and Croatia (away).

Quick Guide England's squad Show Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford, James Trafford, Jason Steele. Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold, Jarrod Branthwaite, Trevoh Chalobah, Marc Guéhi, Lewis Hall, Ezri Konsa, Tino Livramento, Nico O’Reilly, Jarell Quansah. Midfielders: Elliot Anderson, Jude Bellingham, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Alex Scott. Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Eberechi Eze, Anthony Gordon, Harry Kane, Rio Ngumoha, Marcus Rashford, Morgan Rogers, Bukayo Saka. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Tuchel has been unable to include his first-choice right-back, Reece James, or Djed Spence, who can operate in either full-back position, because of injuries. Ben White is also injured; Tuchel said he would have considered him. The centre-half Ezri Konsa, who is in the squad, has played at right-back.

Tuchel said he had spoken to Alexander-Arnold to tell him he would not go to the World Cup but had not called him this time. “He heard the good news over the nomination,” he said. “I am not sure a lot of things have changed. I know what he is capable of. I know about his talent. I know what he is saying: that he is desperate to play for England and he will fight for his shirt. It’s a long camp and it’s a good moment to show up. It’s a chance for Trent to claim what he feels is his – his place on the right side. So here we go.”

Alexander-Arnold was the headline selection on a day when Tuchel gave further recalls to Jarrad Branthwaite, Lewis Hall, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Alex Scott, Cole Palmer and Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He also included Rio Ngumoha. Dean Henderson, John Stones, Dan Burn and Jordan Henderson miss out because of injury. Noni Madueke, Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney have been dropped.

Tuchel overlooked Levi Colwill, Adam Wharton, Phil Foden and Morgan Gibbs-White. Nor was there a recall for Harry Maguire. Tuchel gave the defender hope of involvement at the World Cup when he selected him against Uruguay and Japan in March before he ignored him for the tournament. It drew an outspoken response, Maguire using social media to pronounce himself “shocked and gutted”. His mother, Zoe, said she was “disgusted” by the decision.

Quick Guide How do I 

Of Maguire’s reaction, Tuchel said: “I will not hold it against him for the rest of his life because I’m not that type of person. I can forget easily and quickly. But I didn’t like it and it doesn’t help.”

Tuchel said he had not spoken to Maguire since.

Sports.title: We wanted to let Max Dowman bloom in the shadows but he has become hard to ignore | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
The poet Jorge Luis Borges wrote a famous short story about a society that had become so good at making maps, so obsessed with capturing every detail, that its rulers decided the only way to do the job right was to make a lifesize map of its entire empire, which could then be laid out across the actual land from coast to coast. Imagine a map of Britain the exact same size as Britain, showing every branch of Greggs, every nail bar, every vape shop in perfect detail. Only then can we really see what Britain looks like, by standing on a fake Britain laid over the top of actual Britain.

Borges was writing in the 1940s, at a time when people were fascinated by the mechanised future, with its new forms of measuring out the world: the wireless, the 30mph motorcar, the rise of Big Tape Measure. And to be fair, the mega-map is a pretty accurate vision of our own fully networked present, a place where you can snoop around a village in Mozambique from your laptop in Egham, where no one ever stops committing acts of minute self-surveillance, even if they think they’re just searching “What is beetroot?” on the internet.

Borges also hated football. “Soccer is popular because stupidity is popular,” he wrote, which probably seemed a bold statement at the time. But then Borges also didn’t live to see an episode of Wow Sports Premier League Breakfast at Breakfast with Roger McRoger and a puzzled Lee Trundle. After which, perhaps less of a surprise. But the process he describes is also a good description of what football is doing to itself. Endless data, endless analysis, no spaces or free air, matches that are just schematised movement. At times it can feel like football is out there laying a lifesize real-time map on top of itself.

In Borges’s story, the land soon begins to decay beneath the massive map – which is reassessed by later generations as insane, pointless and stupid – and left to rot in the desert. We haven’t reached this point. Nobody is de-mapping football. But it does perhaps explain why everyone gets so excited when a talent emerges that seems to be playful and human, to exist outside the grid. And also why it has felt wrong to gush too soon about Max Dowman, to fear placing the hex on him. We know how this works. Here is a fluffy new thing. Let us break him. Let us heap pressure on his shoulders. Don’t talk about Max Dowman. Let Max Dowman exist, breathe, bloom in the shadows.

So, Max Dowman then. It has become quite hard to ignore him. He was brilliant against Ipswich in midweek, and brilliant in a way that seems solid and real and comfortable with itself. Most obviously there were the two goals, both a perfect snapshot of why Dowman seems equipped to survive, more state‑of‑the‑art than some other young players we’ve burdened with expectation.

The second goal is particularly good, five perfect little actions packed into six seconds of football. Arsenal have the ball on the edge of the Ipswich box. Dowman shows for a pass, sees it’s going elsewhere, changes his mind, and makes a three-yard sprint to create space. Finally he has the physical capacity to control a bouncing ball in that sliver of space, to move his feet so much quicker than the nearest defender it looks like a glitch in the machine, and to finish in a way that involves sifting the options and timing the shot, all without breaking stride.

View image in fullscreen Max Dowman leaves Cédric Kipré floundering to score his brilliant second, and Arsenal’s third, goal at Ipswich. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

The first goal is on his other side, and involves a more classical piece of one-on-one deception. This is the same defender: Cédric Kipré, 29 years old, came through Paris Saint-Germain’s youth system. Dowman walks through him with a micro-feint and a switch of feet, then reels off another hilariously understated finish, doing it all while a second defender is still gathering himself to lunge, like a man operating in a different time signature to everyone around him.

This is the key point of difference, the ability to make everything stop, the fly-vision that means he sees what’s about to happen while everyone else is whirling about trying to read the charts, in the same way Lionel Messi (yes, sorry, sorry) always seems to have time to pass the ball into the net, like this is all a kickabout in a pair of sliders.

Our way of understanding young creative players has often seemed to lag behind where the game actually is, to be driven by nostalgia for what this thing used to look like. I remember the excitement over the 18-year-old Jack Rodwell’s physicality at the exact moment physicality was no longer going to be a thing, like proudly unveiling the latest horse‑drawn train just as the Ford Model T rolls off the production line.

Michael Owen was brilliant at 17, but he was mainly brilliant at running very fast in a straight line and smashing the ball into the net. Plus of course there was Wayne Rooney, who emerged a pale, unformed teenager composed entirely from energy drinks and white bread, out there making the game up on the fly, as though some urban foundling had come barrelling over the advert boards with a string of sausages still dangling from his mouth.

The narrative around Rooney is that he lost this vital native quality. But Rooney adapted and survived, and clearly understood what he had to be a lot better than those of us watching. And even now creative players have to exist against this. Cole Palmer is exciting because he does surprising things that seem to be striking a blow for freedom, beauty and older people who struggle to make their email work. But his real challenge is to retain just enough of this while fitting the world around him.

Dowman is a bit different. The things that make him stand out seem to speak very easily to how football is now. Being a modern creative footballer is not jinking runs, rasping drives or dribbling across a cabbage field in a pair of cowboy boots. It’s targeted energy, high-intensity semi-freedom. Lamine Yamal and Désiré Doué have the same fast-twitch foot and brain speed, the ability to operate in micro-moments, to see patterns just ahead of time. Dowman is 6ft tall and getting stronger. He won’t be kicked to pieces. He can repeat this without taking bites out of himself.

There is still the issue of his youth. But maybe this doesn’t matter so much either. The world has changed. In the age of Rooney and Owen there was no care, no data, no softness. This is where the structures of modern football are an advantage. Dowman will be GPS’d to the last decimal point. Endless physical scientists will have a say on his output and stress levels.

View image in fullscreen Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as teenagers in an age of less data and less care. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

The money is too big. The talent is too valuable. It also comes ready to plug and play. You don’t get to this level unless you can ingest systems and briefings. You’ve already been pressure-cooked and stress-tested. What you’re being asked to do in the orderly spaces of professional football is the same thing you were asked to do in the orderly spaces of academy football, just five levels up and with more people watching.

Borges was anti-football because he saw it as inauthentic, the players no longer sports people but “actors in jerseys before the TV cameras”. And this is also fine, further evidence that boomer-dad nostalgia is one of the key archetypes of human behaviour.

Life is also different now; not harder or easier, but more instant, a series of moments, the creation of rapid-fire energy. Dowman has grown up inside this. He can parcel his time out, disappear for a bit, maybe make a show of things in the spring.

And yes, this is another way of fitting him to a model, laying a lifesize map of future Max Dowman across the present. But I strongly suspect he will be fine, and that unlike so many other things out there he’s pretty well adapted to whatever the future is supposed to look like.

Sports.title: Uefa and Concacaf ask Gianni Infantino to give Fifa’s billions to its member associations
Sports.content:
The presidents of Uefa and Concacaf have written to Gianni Infantino requesting that Fifa release money from its $6bn (£4.5bn) reserves to its member associations, stating that the plan to fund them via the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme was unnecessary given the cash pile it is sitting on.

Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani proposed a payout of at least $10m to each of Fifa’s 211 member associations (MAs), initially as a one-off during the 2027-2030 commercial cycle. They called for an independent review of Fifa’s financial position and said their own study “raises an important question as to whether the proposed transaction was necessary to deliver greater resources to the MAs”.

The proposed $10m would be handed out on top of money committed by Fifa’s existing Fifa Forward programme, which paid each MA about $8m over the previous four-year cycle. In a separate letter to the presidents of the Asian Football Confederation, the Confederation of African Football, Conmebol (the South American federation) and Oceania, Ceferin and Montagliani asked their counterparts to support the motion. Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the AFC president, is expected to send an endorsement of their plan.

The leaders intend their proposal to be considered at the next Fifa Council meeting on 15 October, where Infantino is due to face Fifa’s nominal decision-making body for the first time since scandal engulfed his reign.

The letter to Infantino states: “Our analysis indicates that Fifa should make at least $10million available to each of its 211 MAs over the 2027-30 cycle for investment in infrastructure and football development – an aggregate of approximately $2.1billion. This would be a one-off release of reserves, over and above the approved Fifa Forward Programme, which would continue in full as already committed.”

It points out Fifa’s reserves would not dip below $1.5bn even after that scale of distribution, and says a larger handout could be possible “once a clearer picture of Fifa’s financial position at year-end is available”.

Ceferin and Montagliani said Fifa “already has the capacity to deliver substantially more to its MAs from its own balance sheet – without any sale of interests in its competitions, and without asking anything of the MAs in return”.

They proceeded to point out that releasing part of Fifa’s reserves would “demonstrate that MAs should not have to choose between development and good governance; between investment and integrity; or between financial support and the ability to consider proposals on their merits. Development is an institutional responsibility of Fifa – not a matter of individual discretion.”

While Fifa Forward Enterprise had promised member associations about $40m, half of that sum was an optional $20m payment for those signing up to his plan.

Infantino remains under pressure to resign but looks certain to run for re-election in March. It remains to be seen whether he will face an opponent.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappé leaves Nike after 20 years to sign boot deal with Swiss brand On
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappé has ended a 20-year association with Nike to sign a boot deal with the Swiss challenger company On.

The sports and leisure brand, which has previously focused on running and tennis, is planning a major move into football next year and has also appointed Thierry Henry as its football director.

Roger Federer, who also left Nike to join them towards the end of his playing career, is a shareholder of the Zurich-based company. Mbappé will also become a shareholder in On.

“From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow’s game,” said the France captain. “I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what’s possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football. We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning.”

On is a newcomer to football and this week unveiled its first boots, the Lightspray Prototype, which will be available for the mass market from next year before a move into training kit.

Mbappé’s departure, which came at the end of his contract after the World Cup, is a significant blow for Nike, which also lost the Barcelona and Spain star Lamine Yamal to Adidas two years ago. The 27-year-old has been the face of many of Nike’s advertising campaigns.

“Kylian’s journey with Nike began when he was nine years old,” the company said in a statement. “Over nearly two decades, we’ve shared moments that shaped the game and he has been an important part of Nike Football. We are proud of what we achieved together on and off the pitch.”

Nike and Adidas dominate the football market with their boots worn by more than 40% of players at this summer’s World Cup, according to data compiled by the retailer Fútbol Emotion, with Puma accounting for about 10%.

Sports.title: Oxford United apologise for launching ‘United 93’ clothing range around 9/11 anniversary
Sports.content:
Oxford United have abandoned a new range of American style-sportswear after it inadvertently referenced the tragedy of September 11.

The League One club launched their new “Campus Collection” on Friday morning but had removed it from sale by lunchtime, after clothing designs were revealed to bear the slogan “United 93”. The U’s immediately published an apology that admitted to a lack of understanding of “the historical context and associations” related to the branding and made “sincere apologies for this error and any offence caused”.

“Inspired by the style and culture of American sports,” the club originally trailed the Campus Collection as launching on 11 September of this year, the 25th anniversary of the atrocity that killed nearly 3,000 people. Concerns over sensitivity saw the launch then delayed, but when the online collection was finally made available for sale on Friday, images showed models wearing an NFL-style shirt with “United 93” on the chest, in recognition of Oxford being founded in 1893.

United 93 was one of four domestic passenger jets seized by al-Qaida terrorists on 11 September 2001. A mutiny by passengers prevented hijackers from using the plane to destroy a government building in Washington DC, and it ultimately crashed into a field, killing all 44 people on board. A film titled “United 93” was also made about the tragedy.

The Campus Collection was live for approximately two hours on Friday before the webpage was deleted by the club after they realised the meaning of the phrase. “The range was released without understanding of the historical context and associations,” the club statement read. “It should not have reached the point of sale and we take full responsibility for not undertaking proper due diligence.

“We have removed the collection with immediate effect and are reviewing our approval processes to ensure nothing like this happens again. Once again, we would like to put on record our sincere apologies for this error and any offence caused.”

Opinion was mixed among Oxford fans, with many outraged but others inclined to forgive the error. One user of the Yellows Forum called it a “monumental cock-up that I would expect to be sacked for if I’d signed off on it”. Another wrote: “Whilst not ideal … everyone who sees this realises there’s no malicious intent. Ultimately there was just no consideration to it at all.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Spying some tasty match-ups, from Wrexham v Saints to desperation derbies
Sports.content:
ENJOY THEM WHILE THEY’RE HOT

Before an engorged international break we have a gala weekend of derby games. Some of them are familiar, others rather longer in the waiting, others spurious in their definition but shoehorned in for tea-timely email purposes. Thursday night’s Bigger Vase defeat by Ferencvaros was not a great result for angry Martin O’Neill’s Celtic, coming three days before the Old Firm/Glasgow derby (delete as applicable according to adherence to Scottish company law), and four days after losing to Rangers in the Old Firm/Glasgow derby. In Spain, Atlético v Real Madrid will see Diego Simeone and José Mourinho bring the morbo ruckus to the sidelines. A football match might actually break out, though that cannot be guaranteed when considering the managers involved.

Plenty of anticipation for Millwall v West Ham, if not from the Met police, which has set up a Section 35 dispersal zone stretching across most of the map on the closing credits of EastEnders. Saturday’s match-up will have rung out when the fixtures came out. That four points separate the two clubs in the battle for promotion has become a side issue. The “Dockers derby”, when supporters’ ancestors worked for rival firms either side of the Thames, hasn’t been played since 2012, the long years since consumed by the cartoon mythology of Danny Dyer, Tamer Hassan and the Rise of the Footsoldier franchise.

Talking of grudge matches, Wrexham v Southampton gained extra Spygate fizz when co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac released a social media disgrace ad for their official web browser (!) on the “importance of privacy”. Those guys! Elsewhere in the Championship, Wolves and West Brom are reunited for a first league fixture in five years, a Sunday high noon kick-off time reflecting West Midlands police’s similar concerns to their London counterparts after a 2024 cup date. Rather more genteel, a university challenge between Oxford and Cambridge, and after Oxon and Cantab split the men’s and women’s Boat Races, there’s first-class honours at stake, in a battle of League One playoff hopefuls.

To a couple of desperation derbies, then. They say you are never more than six feet away from a pest in a big city, and the same logic is true of turmoil at Manchester United and/or Tottenham. Did Michael Carrick shed tears after that Littlewoods Cup defeat by Brighton? Who could blame him? On Sunday United really, really must beat Fulham, for whom Álvaro Arbeloa is taking on the look of lame-duck manager, as well as that of a cross between General Zod and Rylan. If not, Carrick stares down the face of three weeks where “United in crisis” is blood in the water for needy hacks. Maybe Tottenham can provide cover. Their goal drought has been mocked by try-hard pizza companies though perhaps a visit from Aston Villa, whose summer reboot has yielded just one point, can end Spurs’ hosepipe ban.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Scott Murray at 8pm BST for a red-hot updates on Brentford 0-0 Chelsea in yet another weekend derby.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“I got told off for the substitutions I made. Only joking!” – Thomas Tuchel attempts some comedy after being asked what he spoke about with his FA overlords in the post-Geopolitics World Cup review. More impressive was his ability to keep a straight face when he told hacks “99.9% of fans don’t talk about the substitutions I made [against Argentina].” The German recalled Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer in his first squad since the GWC – and even found space for Liverpool’s teenage winger Rio Ngumoha. View the full selection here.

View image in fullscreen Honk! Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

double quotation mark I also met Ludek Miklosko (yesterday’s Football Daily letters), but in a way that now seems rather surreal. When I was a kid, my junior Sunday league team trained at West Ham’s Chadwell Heath training ground every Friday night in their sports hall. In them days, anyone could drive into the car park and walk through the gym to the hall – and on one particular night my dad dropped me and a teammate off and told us he’d be back in an hour. When we walked into the hall we were more than surprised to find that our team had cancelled training, with nobody else turning up, and half of the West Ham first team were in there doing drills instead. With nowhere to go (and no mobile phones) they invited us to join in. As an Arsenal fan, I didn’t really care much for West Ham players, but their goalkeeper was a lovely man and spent most of the hour playing with us and encouraging shots. I never forgot Ludo after that night” – Nicholas Larkin.

double quotation mark I was struck by the sentiment of Christopher D’Cruz that it is not possible to dig yourself out of a hole (yesterday’s letters). OK, I know it is not exactly the same, but it is still a similar principle … they have clearly never heard of Baron Munchhausen pulling himself out of a swamp with his own hair” – Andriy Zavgorodniy.

double quotation mark Christopher has clearly never had to dig a trench, moat, ditch, etc. Sure, there has to be some downward digging to start, but then most of the work is going sideways. Similarly, if you’re stuck at the bottom of a steep-sided hole with nothing but a shovel then the move to get oneself out is digging a gentler slope back to ground-level. Or, to quote the intellectual leviathan, Homer J Simpson: dig up, stupid!” – James Humphries (and 1,056 others).

If you have any, please send letters to the.boss@theguardian.com. Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Nicholas Larkin. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, are here.

Find out which of the Premier League’s sharp shooters are firing their way up the goalscoring charts with our top scorers page, baby. Yep, a certain Norwegian is leading the way again.

Sports.title: Fear and loathing linger as Millwall and West Ham resume ferocious rivalry
Sports.content:
Absence has not made the heart grow fonder. Millwall and West Ham meet for the first time in 14 years on Saturday, but it is not going to be a joyous reunion at the Den. The atmosphere will be ferocious and the main hope is that the focus is on the football rather than any nonsense away from the pitch.

These two have plenty of previous, even though they so rarely play each other. The most glaring example is the shocking disorder inside and outside Upton Park when Millwall lost in the second round of the League Cup at West Ham’s old ground in August 2009. A 44-year-old man was stabbed in the chest as trouble raged outside and riot police struggled to maintain order during the game, with play suspended briefly when home supporters invaded the pitch after one West Ham goal.

View image in fullscreen Police try to control Millwall supporters outside Upton Park station after disturbances following a defeat at West Ham in October 1978. Photograph: PA

There is nothing to glorify here. This will be the 100th competitive meeting, if discontinued, minor tournaments are included, and anyone failing to see the logic behind the rivalry can be forgiven. The sides are not on each other’s doorstep and Millwall are south of the Thames, meaning Crystal Palace and Charlton are more obvious enemies. Yet it is not really about football. The tribalism runs deep, dating back to when the clubs were formed by rival shipbuilding firms at docks on the Isle of Dogs in east London, and is more down to hooligan elements than anything that happens on the pitch.

View image in fullscreen West Ham’s Jack Collison exhorts fans to return to the stands after a pitch invasion at their League Cup tie against Millwall in 2009. Photograph: Stephen Hird/Reuters

There have been many occasions when the nastiness has spiralled out of control. Hooliganism was rife in English football during the 1970s and 1980s and Millwall and West Ham had fearsome firms. Trouble erupted when the sides met at the Den for a testimonial for the Millwall defender Harry Cripps in 1972. The toxicity grew and a Millwall fan, Ian Pratt, died after a clash with West Ham fans at New Cross station in 1976. It is worth keeping in mind when people try to hype up this fixture. Stories about who was top dog on the terraces back in the day are not that interesting.

The 2009 game was disturbing and frightening. In March 2004 there were police horses on the pitch when West Ham fans rioted and ripped up seats during a 4-1 defeat at the Den. Away fans were not allowed in the lower tier when West Ham returned eight months later. West Ham have only 1,774 tickets on Saturday. The Metropolitan police will have measures in place to try to keep opposing fans apart. The dedicated walkway linking South Bermondsey station to the away end acts as a coolant.

The mood will still be tense. There is an odd dynamic to the game. West Ham have at times found it awkward because some of their fans care far more about beating Chelsea and Tottenham. But a trip to Stamford Bridge or N17 is a familiar experience. Going south of the river to Millwall is somehow viewed as different, the short train ride from London Bridge treated as an intrepid journey into some hostile alien planet.

View image in fullscreen Millwall revel in underdog status against West Ham. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

Perhaps the irregularity of the game adds to the mystique. It has happened 18 times in the league since the second world war and only in 1988-89 have the teams been together in the top flight. Millwall stayed up that season but West Ham were relegated, which is usually required for the game to take place. West Ham have generally done something wrong if they are looking for Millwall when the fixture list comes out.

It pits Millwall as underdogs, a role they play well. They often rose to the occasion after West Ham were relegated in 2003. Millwall had a decent team – they reached the FA Cup final in 2004 – and picked up two wins and two draws against West Ham before Alan Pardew led the Hammers back into the Premier League in 2005.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Tim Cahill celebrates Christian Dailly’s own goal as Millwall ran out 4-1 winners at the Den in 2004. Photograph: PA /Alamy

It can be hard for West Ham to match up to the intensity. They won at Upton Park when the sides last met, bouncing back from an early Kevin Nolan red card to beat Millwall in February 2012, but tend to struggle in the away game. The Den is tight, compact, intimidating. Millwall are on a five-match unbeaten run at home against West Ham since losing in 1988. They will look to level the odds. West Ham are on a four-game winning run in the league and top the Championship after smashing Wrexham 6-0 last weekend. Alex Neil’s Millwall came close to winning automatic promotion last season but have injuries and are 10th after an inconsistent start.

Logic says West Ham should win. Logic may not count for very much when the game begins.

Sports.title: UEFA and CONCACAF demand Gianni Infantino hands over £7m to all FIFA members
Sports.content:
UEFA and CONCACAF have written a joint letter to Gianni Infantino calling for at least $10million from its reserves to be paid to FIFA's 211 Member Associations.

It follows Infantino's failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plans, which intended to part-privatise world football's governing body.



4 UEFA and CONCACAF have called on Infantino and FIFA to pay their 211 members using money in their reserves Credit: Getty

The letter is signed by UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin and CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani. The latter is a potential candidate to run against Infantino in next March's election even though he has not yet publicly come forward.

"FIFA is on course to close 2023-26 with reserves of approximately $6billion," reads the letter, seen by talkSPORT. "[This is] considerably more than is required."

Infantino is asked to "make at least $10m available to each of [FIFA's] 211 member associations over the 2027-30 cycle". This would cost $2.11bn with pre-planned funding on top.



The letter backs up a belief from senior UEFA and CONCACAF figures that FIFA should invest using far more of its own reserves.

It was not lost on critics of FFE that Infantino was seeking $4.2bn from investors, including Joshua Kushner, and yet FIFA's own reserves following the 2022 World Cup were almost exactly this number.



Given the investment was offered on such favourable terms to private investors, there appears no reason why FIFA couldn’t have just used its own reserves to fund FFE allowing for 100 per cent of any profits to stay within the organisation. It’s a moot point now FFE has been shelved, but one that has led to a wider debate over how FIFA should use its reserves.

Several federations, including the English Football Association, are in favour of FIFA depleting their reserves in order to better fund members. This is due to FIFA being a not-for-profit organisation and a confidence that the organisation's revenue streams will continue to grow.



Infantino had promised federations who endorsed FFE two joining bonuses: an initial payment worth $20m, and a secondary one for the same amount.

Ceferin and Montagliani argue FIFA has more than enough money to self-fund without the need for private investors.

"FIFA currently holds billions of dollars in accumulated reserves," the letter goes on to read. "These resources belong to football and exist to serve the game and its 211 Member Associations.

4 FIFA have been told to stop withholding 'billions' that currently sit in its reserves Credit: AFP



"Prudence should not prevent a careful examination of whether a portion could responsibly be released to the extent those reserves exceed FIFA's foreseeable needs.

"Releasing part of these reserves would demonstrate that member associations should not have to choose between development and good governance; between investment and integrity; or between financial support and the ability to consider proposals on their merits.

"Development is an institutional responsibility of FIFA – not a matter of individual discretion."

UEFA and CONCACAF have been lobbying other confederations to support their motion ahead of the next FIFA Council meeting on October 15 in Zurich.



Meanwhile, Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has called on Infantino and FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström to release all documents relating to FFE, and to publish the reasoning behind why US striker Flo Balogun's red card against Bosnia was suspended making him eligible to play in the World Cup last sixteen tie with Belgium.

As talkSPORT exclusively revealed, Infantino was lobbied by US President Donald Trump to review the ban.

4 Infantino is under huge pressure after a controversy-filled World Cup and due to his FFE plans Credit: Getty

Infantino has been under significant pressure to stand down following both that incident and the ill-fated FFE proposal. Yet the FIFA President has vowed to fight on, and no candidate has yet come forward to stand against him.



That could change between now and the November 18 deadline, according to UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister. The former Wales international has been one of the leading voices within UEFA pushing for FIFA reforms, including a new president.

'There has to be a challenger for Infantino'

"In the weeks since the exposure of FFE, we have seen a gradual seeping lack of confidence in the leadership of Gianni Infantino," McAllister told talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs at the World Football Summit in Madrid.

"It wasn't just about that initiative, there have been a series of episodes or incidents over recent months and years that have undermined the confidence in his leadership.

"Most recently, there was the overturning of the red card of Balogun at the World Cup, and the FIFA Peace Prize over which there was no consultation… despite it being hugely political.



"There has to be a challenger to Infantino because he will certainly, as he already said, be a candidate in the election unless something dramatic happens in the coming weeks. Of course, it could do, but legal processes [including UEFA putting together a criminal case against Infantino and FIFA] take a long time, so let's not hold our breath over that.

4 UEFA's vice president, McAllister, believes a candidate has to rival Infantino for FIFA presidency Credit: Getty

"There has to be a candidate who, first of all, can command the support of all modernisers beyond just Europe. Football doesn't belong to Europe. Yes, we [UEFA] are a very powerful confederation and, yes, we generate a lot of funds, but football belongs to every single federation and club across the world. On this, I agree with Infantino that football doesn't belong to anyone in any geographical location.

"We have to unite people around a candidate, or maybe more than one candidate, and that candidate, whoever he or she is, has to stand on a manifesto of agreed reform: of greater transparency or greater accountability, of less political interference and must recognise the role of the FIFA President should be to run football, and not [like Infantino] to involve himself in other ventures, whether that's via the private or political sectors.



"I hope very much there will be a candidate [to rival Infantino] and I think that's where we are at the moment. Lots of work is happening behind the scenes. But we need a candidate with an ethos of credibility and modernisation, showing why they should win the election next March."

Behind the scenes, both Infantino and prospective candidates, including Montagliani, are doing the maths to determine where the votes lie.

Infantino went into the 2026 World Cup with 200+ letters of endorsement. Several of these have been revoked, but the FIFA President currently still has more than 106 Member Associations on side despite a wave of withdrawals of support from Europe.

That’s why Infantino remains so bullish about winning another term, but the landscape could yet change if another candidate emerges to rival him.

Sports.title: Harry Kane creates Bundesliga history as he smashes 49-year record for Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Harry Kane creates Bundesliga history as he smashes 49-year record for Bayern Munich

Harry Kane has become the fastest Bundesliga player in history to hit 100 goals.

The England captain scored twice for Bayern Munich against Union Berlin on Friday night to set a German top-flight record.



2 Kane tucked away a penalty for Bayern to reach 100 Bundesliga goals on Friday night Credit: AFP

Kane found the target for the 100th time in the Bundesliga since his 2023 move from Tottenham Hotspur.

He managed to reach a century of goals in just 98 appearances by tucking away a penalty in the 39th minute of the game.

This has smashed the record previously held by German icon Dieter Muller, who took 129 matches to score 100 in 1977 for FC Cologne.



He then went on to score a second time and reach 101 goals, netting another after 54 minutes at the Allianz Arena.

Since joining Bayern three years ago, Kane has remarkably scored a goal every 78.5 minutes in the Bundesliga.



That is a better rate than Erling Haaland and Robert Lewandowski.

In Bayern's last match, a 2-1 win over Elversberg, Kane became the fastest player in their history to hit 150 goals too.

The 33-year-old managed to do so in his 153rd Bayern appearance.

Last season, he scored 61 goals in 51 matches across all competitions and won the European Golden Boot with 36 league strikes.



Closing in on the Ballon d'Or?

Kane is in a strong position for the Ballon d'Or title, with the striker one of the favourites to be crowned at next month's ceremony.

2 Kane smashed home from the spot to reach a century faster than any other player Credit: Getty

Should he win, he would become the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to receive the honour.

And his record-breaking strike is sure to have increased his chances of pipping Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the post.



However, speaking ahead of Friday night's game, where he has made history, he wasn't keen on speaking about the award.

Kane told Marca: “I don’t like to speak about myself… 73 goals speak for themselves.

“It’s been the best season of my life, by far.”

Bayern led 3-0 at half time against Union Berlin, with Kane's penalty the second of the evening in Munich.

Jamal Musiala opened the scoring after 18 minutes before Michael Olise added the third just before the break.



And then Kane added another to double his tally and put Bayern 4-0 up and cruising.

Sports.title: History-making WSL side building new training ground ‘better than most Premier League clubs’
Sports.content:
London City Lionesses owner Michele Kang believes their new training ground will be better than Premier League teams' facilities.

The WSL club, who are the first-ever team not affiliated with a men's side to reach the top flight, are building a new training centre.



3 London City Lionesses are building a new state-of-the-art training ground that will compete with Premier League clubs' Credit: Getty

It is expected to open within the next year, as they continue to take big strides in the women's game under Kang's ownership.

Kang has invested a huge amount of money into the women's football sphere and has transformed London City Lionesses.

Within 18 months of taking over in 2023, they achieved promotion to the WSL, and they've gone from strength to strength since.



Last summer, they broke the women's transfer world record by signing Grace Geyoro from Paris Saint-Germain, before going on to bring in multiple other new superstars this year.

London City Lionesses incredibly brought two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas to the club from Barcelona, also signing her teammate Mapi Leon and ex-England goalkeeper Mary Earps.



As well as investing on the pitch, the club are now in the process of building a new training ground - and it's going to be special.

New training ground 'better than Premier League clubs'

Kang told BBC Sport: "We're building a state-of-the-art training centre for our female athletes dedicated to them, built and designed for them, which will open in less than a year.



"Our architect, who has built several Premier League training centres, told me that by the time the London City training centre is up and running, it would be better than the majority of Premier League men's teams' training centres."

On the importance of making sure the women's game is equal to the men's, she added: "We have to take care of our female players better so that they can train, perform, and thrive as female athletes, not small men.

"You drive your boy to a state-of-the-art training centre and then, if you're lucky enough to have a facility nearby, you drive your girl somewhere else. Why would you accept that?"

3 Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Putellas is London City Lionesses' captain amid investment on and off the pitch Credit: Getty



3 Owner Kang believes the club's new facility will rival some of the best in English football as a whole Credit: Getty

London City Lionesses' new training facility will also help in research into injury rates in the women's game going forward.

"There are more ACL injuries among female players. Two or three times more female players get ACL injuries than male players," Kang continued.

"Something like 94 per cent of all science medical research is dedicated to men. So there's just fundamentally so little known about the female body."



How are London City Lionesses doing this season?

Two games into the WSL season, London City Lionesses are sitting seventh in the table and three points off the top.

They have won one and lost one of their opening games.

In their first game of the league campaign, they beat Manchester United 2-1, as Putellas made her WSL debut.

But a defeat to West Ham followed and now they're preparing to take on Charlton Athletic on Saturday afternoon.

Sports.title: Forgotten ex-Man United defender finds surprise new club after successful trial
Sports.content:
Tyrell Malacia has a new club after leaving Manchester United in the summer with FC Cincinnati snapping him up.

The Dutchman was released by the Red Devils after joining the club from Feyenoord in 2022.



2 Injuries ruined Malacia's time at Old Trafford, and he became the forgotten man Credit: Getty

The left-back has signed a one-year deal with the MLS side after going on trial with the club last week.

Speaking to the club's website about the deal, General Manager Chris Albright said: “We are excited to add a player of Tyrell's experience.

“He's played at the highest levels of the game and knows the demands of competing at that level.



"His quality on the ball, defensive instincts, and desire to win will add to this group and we're happy to welcome him to Cincinnati.”

Lifeline

Malacia arrived at United for around £15million, and he was seen as the eventual replacement for Luke Shaw.



He played an important role for the Red Devils as they made it to the quarter-finals of the Europa League, starting the majority of the games.

In the Premier League, he rotated with Shaw and ended the season having made 39 of the 50 total appearances he managed for Manchester United.



During that season, he also headed to Qatar with the Netherlands squad for the 2022 World Cup.

But the year ended horribly and began an awful period for the defender.

He suffered a knee injury that required surgery ensuring that he didn't play at all during the 2023/24 campaign.

2 Malacia was released at the end of last season and has been searching for a club since Credit: Getty



The following year saw him return from injury only to be loaned out to PSV Eindhoven in the second half of the season.

During that season, Malacia publicly spoke about his injury hell.

He said: “We spoke to the guy who did my [first knee] surgery and then we made the decision: we had to do something else. I had to start my rehab over, basically… I had one day to be disappointed.

"Then I had to be like, ‘OK, we go again’. I think at the end of the day, everything I did, even if it was a mistake or something, I won’t even see it as a mistake because it’s a lesson.

"I think everything in life is already written for me. I had to go through this whole process to be where I’m at now, so I wouldn’t do anything different."



In the 2025/26 campaign, Malacia managed just 15 minutes for United's first team.

But having now secured a move to Cincinnati, Malacia will hope he can get his career back on track.

Sports.title: Arsenal told they could go invincible again thanks to vital ingredients
Sports.content:
Arsenal told they could go invincible again thanks to vital ingredients

Arsenal have the right manager with the right mindset to go invincible for the second time in the Premier League.

That's the view of former Gunners left-back Ashley Cole who feels they have created the perfect environment for glory.

5 Arteta's side are already winning by any means necessary, as they did last season Credit: Getty

Arsenal, led by the fiercely determined Mikel Arteta, won the title last season by seven points ahead of Man City.

It saw the apprentice finally get the better of the master as Pep Guardiola failed to fend off his fellow Spaniard.

In previous campaigns, the Gunners were superb challengers but gained a reputation for losing their nerve at the vital moment.

Last term though, they were ruthless in pursuit of their first title since 2004, when the team, which Cole played in, went unbeaten and earned their Invincibles tag.

As such, while they lost one extra game last season, they managed to get into the habit of turning draws into wins.

And if they continue to build on that habit with their impressive mindset, Cole doesn't think an unbeaten season is out of their reach having already won all of their first four games.

He told talkSPORT at the launch event of the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 Hobby Box in Fanatics Collectibles on Regent Street: "I don't see why not.

"I think Mikel has had that group now for four or five years. He's been allowed to bring in his own players and take players out.

"I think they've created a great environment where players understand now is about winning. You've got to continue to keep winning.

"They are the champions, so they are going to go into the season, which they've already shown, with a personality, a belief, a desire and a hunger to not just regain the Premier League, but can they do more in the Champions League? They had a taste of that last season and fell a little bit short. They had a great season last year, but you always want to better what you did the previous season.

5 Cole was speaking at the launch event of the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 Hobby Box in Fanatics Collectibles on Regent Street Credit: Topps

5 Arsenal won the Premier League title last season and celebrated in style Credit: Getty

"So, big boots to fill, but I think they've got the players, the squad, the mentality, the environment to do it.

"Can they go unbeaten? It's not easy, but they have got the players and I think they've got the manager with the mindset now. So, who knows?"

Cole, speaking at the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 Hobby Box launch was once a keen collector himself.

Now his son is doing the same and Cole spoke about the joy of a new generation finding his cards.

He added: "I've got big memories of collecting. I think every little bit of pocket money I had, I would go into the local shop and buy the cards and spend the whole day putting them in the sticker books, whether it's a sticker or a card, where you put them in a little case.

"It's definitely something I always did as a child and now I have a son, 10 years of age, and he loves it.

5 Cole opened hobby boxes of the Topps Flagship Premier League 2026/27 set with the SideCards crew at Fanatics Collectibles Credit: Topps

"It's like going back to my childhood and now I help him swap and exchange cards and he also picked me out as well, so that was quite incredible."

Asked about the experience of seeing himself in a collection, he replied: "It's quite crazy really because as a young boy I never thought I'd be in the position where I would play for my boyhood club and then actually seeing myself on a card wearing a shirt. It is absolutely mind-blowing.

"Then 20, 30 years down the line, now I have my own kids and I still see my name and see my card and see my face on the card in different shirts. It's incredible and I look back now and think, I lived out a dream and it's still continuing by having my face on these cards."

Things are a bit different now with Topps innovating within the industry.

Autographed cards and cards with shirt patches inside are now chased by fans and Cole loves that they can now own a piece of their favourite star's history.

He added: "It's incredible how they've evolved and developed.

5 Cole joined fans at the launch event for Topps' Flagship Premier League 2026/27 Hobby Boxes Credit: Topps

"Now you get the opportunity to get a card with an authentic piece of shirt on it. It's mind-boggling to understand that that can fit on a card and you can have a part of that player's journey with the picture signed from the player.

"It's brilliant. I think it just adds a different layer to it and a better layer and now you become part of that player's career as well, which I think is special."

Sports.title: Alexander Isak risks further Newcastle anger after declaring it was ‘easy decision’ to leave
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak risks further Newcastle anger after declaring it was ‘easy decision’ to leave

Alexander Isak has revealed that it was an 'easy' decision to leave Newcastle United and join Liverpool, and he regrets nothing.

The Swedish international departed the Magpies on transfer deadline day to join the Reds in a British record £125million deal last year.



4 Isak has three goals so far in his second season at Liverpool after joining the club from Newcastle in controversial circumstances Credit: Getty

However, the move was far from amicable.

After helping the Magpies win the Carabao Cup and qualify for the Champions League, Isak refused to play in any of Newcastle's pre-season games.

He spent part of the summer training away from the club in an effort to force a move away from Tyneside.

Newcastle rejected a couple of offers from Liverpool and the season started with Isak refusing to play in the first three games of the year.



The striker released a bombshell statement at one point in which he claimed the club had broken some promises to him.

In the end, Newcastle managed to sign Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa, allowing Isak to complete his transfer to Liverpool.



And in his first proper sit-down interview of the season with the BBC, Isak insists he made the right decision.

What has Isak said on his Newcastle exit?

Isak admitted: "[Liverpool] is a massive club, and everything about the club made it an easy decision.



"And the club's ambition and the club's will to get me in as well. It was a big part of it.

Asked if he regretted the switch, he added: "No, never. I would never think like that."

4 Isak was one of the best strikers in the world at Newcastle and is looking to rediscover this form again Credit: Getty

4 Isak is the main frontman for Liverpool under Andoni Iraola with Hugo Ekitike out Credit: Getty



Bouncing back

After missing all of Newcastle's pre-season to force through his move to Anfield, Isak was well short of fitness.

The 26-year-old's first start in the Premier League for Liverpool came at the end of September against Crystal Palace.

He didn't score a top-flight goal until the end of November against West Ham.

Isak then suffered a broken leg while scoring against Tottenham after a Micky van de Ven tackle in a desperate attempt to stop the goal.



But Van de Ven accidentally crunched Isak, and he returned near the end of the year to score one more goal against Palace at Anfield.

Speaking about that injury, Isak said: "[The leg break] was tough. Anyone who had a long injury would know. But on the other hand, when you're in a good place and when you feel good, you don't really tend to look back because it doesn't really benefit you. So I'm just looking forward and feel really optimistic and excited about the season, and what it can bring to us."

4 Isak has already matched his Premier League goal tally from last year Credit: Getty

Mixed start

The opening game of the season saw Isak return to St James' Park for the first time since his move.



He was booed throughout and called a 'rat' by the Toon fans, who rather enjoyed his miss in the second half during the 2-2 draw.

Isak then scored at home to Nottingham Forest and grabbed a double in a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town.

In that match, he looked much more like the Isak of old, but since then, he's blanked against Atletico Madrid and Fulham.

However, Isak believes Liverpool will go on to have a great season.

"Everyone knows that success for this club is winning trophies. I want to score every game. Everyone is different. Some like to set targets and some don't. I'm the one that doesn't."

Sports.title: EFL star tipped for Thomas Tuchel’s Euro 2028 squad despite being uncapped for England
Sports.content:
EFL star tipped for Thomas Tuchel’s Euro 2028 squad despite being uncapped for England

Adrian Durham has backed uncapped Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear to lead the line for England at Euro 2028.

Lankshear has shone following his summer move from Tottenham Hotspur to the Riverside, netting six goals for this title-challenging Boro side.



3 Lankshear has been banging the goals in for fun this season since joining Middlesbrough on a permanent switch from Tottenham Credit: Getty

The youngster's stock has soared considerably since leaving the capital outfit, who are yet to score a Premier League goal this season.

And speaking on Hawksbee & Jacobs, Durham believes that England boss Thomas Tuchel, who named his squad for the extended international break on Friday, will soon turn to the 21-year-old.

'He reminds me of Harry Kane'

"I really am a big fan of this guy," the talkSPORT stalwart began on Friday.



"I think had he gone to a lower Premier League side instead of Middlesbrough, he might have been in this squad.

"I think he is going to be the real deal.

"I've said this before on a Fiery Fridays talkSPORT daily, he is going to be an England striker. He'll probably even be at the Euros.



"I think he's brilliant. He has got the numbers, but it's more to his game than that.

"He can back it up with how he plays. I don't think he's got electric pace.



"In so many ways, he does remind me of Harry Kane.

"I'm not saying he's that good before anybody rings in, but I think he's got the potential to go on and be an England number nine of the future."

3 Lankshear will win an England cap before long, according to Durham Credit: Getty

Durham's previous Lankshear comments

Speaking on Fiery Fridays last month, Durham said that he felt Spurs would come to regret cashing in on Lankshear.

And ahead of the weekend's Premier League action, Durham's comments ring true.



That's because Spurs are one of two sides, along with newly promoted Coventry City, yet to score a league goal this season, while last season's top scorer, Richarlison, has been axed from the squad by head coach Roberto De Zerbi.

"Spurs selling Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough, I think will go down as the worst mistake any Premier League club has ever made," Durham said.

"I think even by the end of this season, Spurs will be regretting what I think is a crazy decision.

"Lankshear will play for England before the season is out. He’ll be an Arsenal player this time next year. For the second time in their recent history, Spurs have just sold Harry Kane."



3 Lankshear has scored more competitive goals than former side Spurs this season Credit: Getty

Durham continued: "Unless Spurs add goals before the end of the transfer window [on 1 September], they will be watching Will Lankshear, their product, smash in 20-plus [goals] for Boro, wishing he could be doing the same for them because Tottenham will need ways to find the back of the net.

"Last season, Lankshear scored double figures for a poor side in the Championship. His numbers at Oxford United were better than anything Harry Kane achieved in his loan spells as a young Spurs player.

"What I like about his play is, if you’ve not seen him play, he’s not just goals. He’s got many qualities. I’ve seen him described as a penalty box striker and he converts chances, he is a finisher for sure.



"Like any striker, most of his goals are scored in the box. I’ve seen him score from distance. He’s capable of the spectacular. He’s calm, movement is a bit special, strong, good in the air. He makes terrific runs. He can assist as well."
